morphology_entries.coding_note: Chain terminator for every /0 chain in this file: nos_fallback_code is null by design. Authored at /0, /1 and /3 only -- 8000/6 and 8000/9 exist in ICD-O-3.2 but sit outside the group's 0-1,3 declaration and would drop a case out of Group III silently (Revision 2 §1.3 trap 1, §4.16). NOTE: the /0 chain terminates here rather than continuing to 8000/1 because build_database.py's check_fallback_chains keys the fallback graph by morphology_code alone; 8000/0 -> 8000/1 reads as a self-reference and FAILs. Reached on a demonstrated benign intracranial or intraspinal mass with no established histogenesis. Record the five-point IIIf flag (§4.16): surgery, tissue sent, IHC requested, result unavailable or not requested, and the ENCR basis of diagnosis.

morphology_entries.coding_note: ICCC-3 constrains 8158 to C75.1 -- Revision 2 §4.11 corrects the previous revision's claim that it is site-agnostic. ACTH-producing tumour. The fallback is 8272/0 Pituitary adenoma, NOS and NOT 8272/3: §4.11 rules that malignant behaviour in the pituitary requires demonstrated craniospinal or systemic metastasis and that no histological feature qualifies, so a tool that lets an untested ACTH-producing tumour fall to a carcinoma code manufactures pituitary carcinomas. ENCR Table 4 gives a basis-4 route: a functioning pituitary tumour diagnosed on GH/FSH/LH/ACTH/TSH codes 8272/0.
morphology_entries.topography_routing_note: IIIe1 only at C75.1. ICCC-3 constrains 8158 and 8290 to C75.1; at any other topography they leave Group III and route to Group XI. 8270-8281 and 8300 carry no such constraint and are IIIe1 at any site. Revision 2 §4.11 corrects the previous revision, which called these codes site-agnostic.

morphology_entries.coding_note: Tinctorial classification (chromophobe/acidophil/basophil), superseded by the transcription-factor scheme of Sood 2024 and Korbonits 2024: first-tier PIT1, TPIT, SF-1, hormone stains second-tier, lineage reachable at RL III. Code as documented in the file; do not assign prospectively -- a new case gets 8272/0 with the lineage recorded as an annotation, which is code-neutral (8272/0 carries corticotroph, somatotroph, gonadotroph, thyrotroph, plurihormonal and null cell adenoma as Related terms).

Tinctorial legacy string at /3. See 8270/0. Imaging is in the required set because §4.11 makes demonstrated metastasis -- craniospinal or systemic -- the only thing that establishes malignant behaviour in this subgroup. Ki-67 >3%, p53 positivity and invasion make a tumour aggressive, not malignant.

ICD-O-3.2's preferred term is 'Lactotroph adenoma', NOT 'Prolactinoma' -- prolactinoma is a clinical term (Revision 2 §4.11). One of the 15 preferred terms §1.1b records as not in circulation among abstractors, so the alias file must not assume it has been seen. ENCR Table 4 basis-4 route: a prolactinoma diagnosed on prolactin codes here, at /0.

The pituitary family NOS and the recode destination for the obsolete pituitary codes 8040, 8140, 8146 and 8260 at C75.1 (Revision 2 §4.11). Lineage assignment by PIT1 / TPIT / SF-1 is code-neutral: corticotroph, somatotroph, gonadotroph, thyrotroph, plurihormonal, null cell and ectopic pituitary adenoma are all Related terms of this code in ICD-O-3.2. CNS5 uses the term PitNET but notes it is 'further debated' and ICD-O-3.2 has no PitNET string; keep 8272 and annotate.

Pituitary carcinoma, NOS. §4.11: malignant behaviour requires demonstrated metastasis, craniospinal or systemic. No histological feature qualifies -- not Ki-67 >3%, not p53 positivity, not invasion. Imaging is a required test because it is what demonstrates the metastasis. A tool that lets atypia drive /3 will manufacture pituitary carcinomas.

Pituitary blastoma, NOT 'Oncocytoma, NOS' -- the string '8273 - Oncocytoma, NOS' is in circulation and is not an ICD-O-3.2 term at all (§1.1b); it is an alias input only. One of the two codes Revision 2 supplies diagnostic content for that the previous revision left blank (§1.6). An embryonal neoplasm of infancy: Liu 2021, all 17 reported cases 24 months or younger, median 11 months; ACTH IHC positive in 16/17; DICER1 alteration in 16/17. The only malignant /3 pituitary code that is a paediatric entity. The DICER1 germline implication is code-neutral and belongs in clinical-warnings.md, not here (ruling 9). Fallback is 8000/3, not 8272/3: a blastoma is not a carcinoma and 8272/3 would assert a metastasis that has not been demonstrated.

morphology_entries.coding_note: ICCC-3 constrains 8290 to C75.1 (§4.11). The ICD-O-3.2 Related term that matters here is 'Spindle cell oncocytoma' -- §4.12 names it the third member of the TTF-1-positive neurohypophyseal family alongside 9432/1 pituicytoma and 9582/0 granular cell tumour of the sellar region, which CNS5 groups in one section but classifies separately. It sits in IIIe1 by code while its two siblings sit in IIIe2. The other Related terms (Hurthle cell adenoma, follicular adenoma oxyphilic cell) are thyroid terms and are unreachable inside the C75.1 constraint. The string 'Oncocytic adenoma' is in circulation against a code ICD-O-3.2 does not carry at all; the TERM belongs here and that pairing is an alias input only. The sixteen codes in the inventory's codes_absent_from_icdo32 are deliberately not written out anywhere in this file (Revision 2 §6.6 rule 7).

morphology_entries.nos_fallback_name: Neoplasm, uncertain whether benign or malignant
morphology_entries.coding_note: Craniopharyngioma has no malignant form in ICD-O-3.2 -- 9350, 9351 and 9352 are /1 only. Under a malignant-only registration rule it disappears from the registry entirely, which is why site_profile.registry_policy.register_nonmalignant_cns is true (Revision 2 §1.3, §1.7). ENCR Table 3 permits 9350/1 at C75.2 on imaging alone (basis 2): a calcified suprasellar cystic mass, over 90% calcified in children. That route is an ENCR registration allowance, not an imaging-sufficient endpoint in this tool -- imaging_sufficient is true on exactly two entries (9440/3 and 9421/1) and this is not one of them.

Fukuhara 2021: 26 of 38 adamantinomatous cases were beta-catenin IHC positive, but only 11 of those 26 (42%) carried a demonstrable CTNNB1 mutation on sequencing. The paper's conclusion is that beta-catenin immunostaining was more positive than CTNNB1 mutations -- IHC is more sensitive than sequencing here, the shortfall attributed to sampling, and the authors rule that IHC suffices. All 12 children in that series were adamantinomatous. This is one of the few places in Group III where the IHC branch should be preferred over the molecular one.

Fukuhara 2021: BRAF VE1 IHC positive in 11/11 papillary cases (100%). Papillary craniopharyngioma is an adult tumour; in a paediatric registry 9352 should be rare and a case coded here is worth a soft review flag (Revision 2 §4.12). The flag is clerk-facing and belongs in the branch's reason or hint, never here -- coding_note is not displayed.

morphology_entries.nos_fallback_name: Neoplasm, uncertain whether benign or malignant
morphology_entries.coding_note: Pinealoma is a legacy string; CNS5 recognises pineocytoma, PPTID, pineoblastoma and papillary tumour of the pineal region, not 'pinealoma'. It is the /1 hub for this subgroup only because it is the least specific /1 pineal code. Li 2020 governs the whole subgroup: 22.6% (21/93) of institutional pineoblastoma diagnoses were other entities, commonest germ cell tumours, and the 34.4% marker-negative rate means the AFP/beta-hCG rule of §3.2 is not sufficient on its own.

morphology_entries.nos_fallback_name: Neoplasm, uncertain whether benign or malignant
morphology_entries.coding_note: Pineocytoma. A pineal tumour needs tissue plus INI1 plus germ cell markers (Revision 2 §4.13) -- AT/RT is common in the pineal region and desmoplastic myxoid tumour of the pineal region, SMARCB1-mutant also loses INI1. The AFP / beta-hCG rule of §3.2 is one-directional: elevated refers to Group X and stops; normal proceeds to tissue with germ cell tumour still live. Never apply one compartment's cut-off to the other (beta-hCG CSF 8.2 IU/L, alphaFP serum 25 ng/mL) and capture the number, not a yes/no. nos_fallback re-pointed from 9360 (obsolete in ICD-O-3.2) to 8000/1 on 2026-09-14.

Pineoblastoma and pineal parenchymal tumour of intermediate differentiation share this code -- PPTID, 'Mixed pineal tumor' and 'Transitional pineal tumor' are all Related terms of 9362/3. Pineoblastoma molecular subgroups require methylation profiling and sequencing, no IHC surrogate exists, and every subgroup is 9362/3 regardless, so code_neutral_molecular is true and the tool must not build the branch (§4.13). Fallback is 8000/3, not 9473/3: ICCC-3 files pineoblastoma in IIIe3, and routing it into the embryonal family would move the case between subgroups.

THE INTRA-GROUP TOPOGRAPHY SPLIT, and the only entry in this file carrying iccc3_subgroup_by_topography (contract §1.3). ICCC-3 puts 9380/3 in IIIb at C72.3 and in IIId2 everywhere else in the group -- one (code, behaviour) pair with two subgroups, where check_duplicate_code_behavior_pairs allows only one entry and renderOutput() reads iccc3_subgroup_id straight off it. The entry's own subgroup is the default, IIId2, the larger destination; the ordered rule overrides to IIIb at C72.3. primary_sites is the UNION of the two ICCC-3 rows (C70.0-C72.2 + C72.3 + C72.4-C72.9, collapsed to C70.0-C72.9, plus C75.1 and C75.3) so the entry stays total across both destinations. 9380 has EXACTLY TWO terms in ICD-O-3.2 -- 'Glioma, malignant' and 'Glioma, NOS' -- and fourteen strings in circulation wrongly attach it to 9400's terms; every one of those is an alias pointing at 9400/3 (§1.1b). This is the workhorse NOS code for a glial tumour whose lineage is not established, and the hub every glial family chain passes through on its way to 8000/3.
morphology_entries.topography_routing_note: ICCC-3 routes 9380 to IIIb at C72.3 (optic nerve) and to IIId2 at every other CNS site. The entry's own subgroup is the default (IIId2, the larger destination); the rule above overrides it when the captured topography is C72.3.

morphology_entries.iccc3_subgroup_name: Neuroepithelial glial tumors of uncertain origin
morphology_entries.coding_note: LIVE CODE, RETIRED DIAGNOSIS. Gliomatosis cerebri is a GROWTH PATTERN, not a type (§1.2). Imaging is in the required set because the multi-lobar extent that the term describes is an imaging finding, not a histological one. Code historical files as documented; never assign prospectively.

LIVE CODE, RETIRED DIAGNOSIS. Oligoastrocytoma was deleted by WHO 2016 and not restored (§1.2). Code historical files as documented; NEVER assign prospectively. One of the 15 preferred terms §1.1b records as not in circulation; '9382 - Oligoastrocytoma' without the ', NOS' suffix is not an ICD-O-3.2 term and is an alias input only.

RL I: H&E alone fulfils the CNS5 essential criteria and Satgunaseelan calls the RL III surrogate IHC 'unnecessary' (Revision 2 §4.0). ihc_markers_required is null for that reason. Subependymoma must be excluded on morphology BEFORE H3 K27me3 is interpreted in the posterior fossa -- it retains the stain, as does myxopapillary ependymoma, and update 11 records that the PF-SE methylation class mimics retained K27me3 (§4.1). Fallback is 9391/3 Ependymoma, NOS: there is no ependymal NOS code at /0 or /1, so the behaviour rises from /1 to /3 at the fallback. That is a property of ICD-O-3.2, not a choice; 9391/1 is Sellar ependymoma, a distinct entity, not a /1 NOS.

Subependymal giant cell astrocytoma. Revision 2 gives no IHC panel for it, so ihc_markers_required is null rather than invented; the diagnosis rests on morphology, the foramen of Monro location and the tuberous sclerosis context. Fallback 9400/3 Astrocytoma, NOS -- the astrocytic NOS code, which ICD-O-3.2 carries at /3 only, so the behaviour rises at the fallback.

Diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27M-mutant -- CNS5 calls it H3 K27-ALTERED; ICD-O-3.2 still says H3 K27M-mutant. Related term 'Diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma, H3 K27M-mutant'. This is where a molecularly confirmed DIPG belongs: IIId2, NOT IIIb. H3 K27M IHC is the single highest-value stain in this group -- an RL III marker that names a WHO CNS5 type outright and changes the code from 9440/3 to 9385/3, which is exactly the test-availability artefact of §1.5: the same tumour lands in a different ICCC-3 subgroup depending on whether one immunostain was available. The fallback is 9440/3 for that reason. CNS5 Table 2 lists H3 K27, TP53, ACVR1, PDGFRA, EGFR and EZHIP for this entity; the non-defining members of that list are captured without changing the code. THE MIS-BRANCH TO WATCH: an H3 K27M-positive tumour with ependymoma morphology and dot-like EMA is PFA EPENDYMOMA, not diffuse midline glioma (§4.1) -- which is why EMA is an exclusion here. One of the 15 preferred terms not in circulation.

One code, three behaviours, three different tumours -- BLOCKING in Revision 2 §4.2, and the reason this file authors three separate objects. A downstream system that records only a four-digit code cannot tell 9390/0 papilloma from 9390/3 carcinoma, so behaviour must survive to whatever consumes the output (§1.7). Kir7.1 and transthyretin support choroid plexus origin against ependymoma; an EMA dot-pattern supports ependymoma and is therefore an exclusion here. Reachable at RL II-III. Fallback is 8000/0 and not 9390/0-family: check_fallback_chains keys by morphology_code alone, so any within-code behaviour fallback (9390/1 -> 9390/0) reads as a self-reference and FAILs. All three behaviours therefore point at 8000, which keeps the collapsed graph consistent.

morphology_entries.nos_fallback_name: Neoplasm, uncertain whether benign or malignant
morphology_entries.coding_note: Atypical choroid plexus papilloma is defined by ONE criterion: 2 or more mitoses per 10 HPF of 0.23 mm-squared. Nothing else is required. Record the denominator with the count -- this group states mitotic thresholds in five incompatible units and a band list without a denominator is a build error (contract §2(7): unit per_10_hpf, hpf_area_mm2 0.23). The prognostic meaning of the atypical category VANISHES below age 3, which is the age band where most paediatric choroid plexus tumours occur, so record the grade-2 call and do not over-weight it. Fallback 8000/1: see 9390/0.

Choroid plexus carcinoma: 4 or more of 5 criteria, including more than 5 mitoses. The 40-50% association with Li-Fraumeni syndrome and the germline TP53 testing requirement are a clinical alert, so under ruling 9 they live in docs/clinical-warnings.md and clinical_alert is null here; the germline finding is code-neutral. Fallback is 8000/3, not 9390/0: a carcinoma must not fall back onto a papilloma code, and check_fallback_chains would read the within-code hop as a self-reference in any case.

Sellar ependymoma. One of the 15 preferred terms §1.1b records as not in circulation among abstractors, and flagged in the §1.1 inventory. It cannot fall back to 9391/3 Ependymoma, NOS: build_database.py's check_fallback_chains keys the fallback graph by morphology_code alone, so 9391/1 -> 9391/3 reads as a self-reference and FAILs. It therefore skips to 9380/3 Glioma, malignant, the same destination 9391/3 uses, which keeps both behaviours of code 9391 pointing at one target code.

The ependymal family hub and the single most overloaded code in the group. CNS5 defines five ependymoma types that need it -- ST ZFTA fusion-positive (where the fusion is not proven), ST YAP1 fusion-positive, PF group PFA, PF group PFB and SP MYCN-amplified -- and morphology code alone cannot distinguish them, so code_neutral_molecular is true and every case carries an entity annotation (§1.4, option A). It is also where update 11's three orphan NEC labels land. Branch-level, not entry-level, markers: H3 K27me3 loss (>80% of cells negative) gives PFA in the posterior fossa -- Panwalkar 2017 states 99% sensitivity / 100% specificity but its raw counts give 100% / 97.5% (72/72 PFA negative, 39/40 PFB positive, n=112 with methylation data from 230 tumours across 22 institutions); cite both and report the raw counts. Retained K27me3 does NOT give PFB -- update 11 demotes it to desirable only and requires DNA methylation profiling, so there is no IHC-only path to PFB. EZHIP (Nambirajan 2021: sensitivity 72% (23/32), specificity 100%, PPV 100%, NPV 70%) is mutually exclusive with H3 K27M. L1CAM and p65/RelA are used NEGATIVELY only: double-negative excludes ZFTA (NPV 100%, n=42) and they cannot assert it (single-marker PPV 73-91.7%). Reject Lim 2022's rule that all L1CAM-positive cases are ZFTA-positive. These are entry-level absent deliberately: H3 K27me3 refines within this one code, so listing it as required would report a phantom outstanding test on every supratentorial and spinal ependymoma.

CNS5 DELETED anaplastic ependymoma as a type -- grade is now expressed within the type. The code is live in ICD-O-3.2 and ICCC-3, so code historical files as documented; never assign prospectively. Ceiling is low for that reason, not because the histology is hard.

One of the eight codes Revision 2 §1.6 records as having had no diagnostic content anywhere in the previous revision, and one of the six that remain legacy strings. CNS5 demoted papillary, clear cell and tanycytic ependymoma from subtypes to morphological PATTERNS, which is consistent with ICD-O-3.2: clear cell, cellular and tanycytic ependymoma are Related terms of 9391/3 and only papillary kept its own code. Treat 9393/3 as a legacy string; a papillary pattern in an ependymoma is 9391/3.

RL II -- GFAP positivity completes the diagnosis (Revision 2 §4.0). CNS5 moved myxopapillary ependymoma from grade 1 to GRADE 2. Filum/conus. It retains H3 K27me3, so it must be excluded on morphology before K27me3 is interpreted (§4.1). Below RL II the rendered diagnosis is 'suggestive of MPE, NOS', grade II, on the descriptive track; the code fallback is 9391/3 because ICD-O-3.2 has no ependymal NOS at /1.

Papillary tumour of the pineal region is defined by a methylation class and no IHC panel for it appears in any source in this corpus (Revision 2 §4.13) -- ihc_markers_required is null for that reason, not by omission. An RL V entity with a strong ependymoma mimic: 10 of 34 PTPR-B cases had previously been diagnosed as ependymoma. 'Molecular/PCR' is the closest member of the closed test vocabulary to methylation profiling, which has no member of its own; the contract declares methylation_counts_as 8 for ENCR basis.

The only molecularly defined ependymoma code in ICD-O-3.2, and it names the fusion partner RELA, which CNS5 and cIMPACT-NOW updates 9 and 11 have replaced with ZFTA (§1.2). RL IV: 'definite diagnoses cannot be made by surrogate markers alone'. diagnostic_tests_required names Cytogenetics/FISH and not Molecular/PCR because the list has no OR semantics and the engine subtracts from it literally -- §4.0 gives the route as 'FISH or RT-PCR', so the RT-PCR branch in the tree must declare satisfies_tests ['Cytogenetics/FISH'] rather than the entry dropping a requirement. L1CAM is required as supporting evidence only: with p65/RelA it excludes ZFTA when both are negative (NPV 100%) and cannot assert the fusion. Chinnam 2022's two-of-three rule (any two of L1CAM, p65, cyclin D1) lifts sensitivity 92.3% to 96.2% and NPV to 96.6%. YAP1 fusion-positive ST ependymoma has no positive IHC surrogate with any performance data and stays at 9391/3 -- do not reuse the medulloblastoma YAP1 marker token here, the two are unrelated (§4.1).

The low-grade astrocytic hub. ICD-O-3.2 carries 'Diffuse astrocytoma, IDH-mutant' and 'Diffuse astrocytoma, IDH-wildtype' as Related terms of this code, so IDH status is captured without changing the code -- code_neutral_molecular true. Fourteen strings in circulation attach 9380 to this code's terms (Astrocytoma NOS, Diffuse astrocytoma, Cystic astrocytoma, Astroglioma, Astrocytic glioma, Astrocytoma low grade, Diffuse astrocytoma low grade); 9380 has exactly two terms in ICD-O-3.2, 'Glioma, malignant' and 'Glioma, NOS', so the alias file must send every one of them here (§1.1b). This is also the code every paediatric-type diffuse glioma with no ICD-O-3.2 code falls to when it is low grade -- PLNTY, diffuse astrocytoma MYB/MYBL1-altered, diffuse low-grade glioma MAPK pathway-altered -- with the CNS5 entity recorded as an annotation (§4.3). H3 K27M must be negative or the code is 9385/3.

Anaplastic astrocytoma. ICD-O-3.2 carries 'Astrocytoma, anaplastic, IDH-mutant' and 'IDH-wildtype' as Related terms, so IDH status is code-neutral here too. cIMPACT-NOW update 11 is universal inside this registry (age bound 18, Revision 2 §1.7): TERT promoter mutation is not a solitary defining feature in a histologically low-grade tumour at any age, and EGFR amplification and +7/-10 are not solitary defining features below 40 -- in a child none of the three stands alone, so never build a solitary-criterion branch. Update 11 also says MMR IHC (MSH2, MSH6, MLH1, PMS2) 'should be considered' in patients under 18 with H3-wildtype high-grade glioma, including IDH-mutant astrocytoma; that is the weakest of the three tiers and must not be rendered as obligatory.
Protoplasmic astrocytoma: a histological subtype CNS5 no longer recognises. Code historical files as documented; never assign prospectively.
morphology_entries.obsolete_source: IARC ICD-O-3.2 morphology table (ICD-O-3.2_final_update09102020.xls, sha256 7ca51dcb...78a21), column 'obs' = [obs]. No non-obsolete term exists for this code at this behaviour. Removed from the decision tree by registrar's ruling, 2026-09-14; retained here so historical records and alias input still resolve.

morphology_entries.coding_note: Gemistocytic astrocytoma, NOS: a histological subtype CNS5 no longer recognises, and one of the 15 preferred terms §1.1b records as not in circulation. The string '9411 - Gemistocytic astrocytoma' in circulation is not an ICD-O-3.2 term at all and is an alias input only -- the ICD-O-3.2 term carries the ', NOS' suffix.

Desmoplastic infantile astrocytoma; Related term 'Desmoplastic infantile ganglioglioma', so DIA and DIG share this code and the fallback stays in the glioneuronal family at 9505/1. Ki-67 is under 2% despite an alarming size. CONGENITAL GLIOBLASTOMA IS ABOLISHED (Gilani 2023): those tumours are infant-type hemispheric gliomas or DIG/DIA, and histology alone cannot separate them -- 2 of 5 histological DIG/DIA in that series were IHG. Infant-type hemispheric glioma has no ICD-O-3.2 code; it needs an RTK fusion (ALK, ROS1, NTRK, MET) or the IHG methylation class, and its fallback rendering is 'IHG-DIG spectrum, NOS' -- NEVER 'congenital glioblastoma' (§4.3).

Dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumour, /0, and one of the two commonest tumours in paediatric drug-resistant epilepsy surgery series (with ganglioglioma). A malignant-only registration rule erases the entire low-grade epilepsy-associated tumour population, which is §4.14's strongest argument for register_nonmalignant_cns true. Revision 2 names no DNET-specific IHC panel, so ihc_markers_required is null by decision. The differential that matters is MVNT (CNS5 grade 1, no ICD-O-3.2 code): H&E vacuolated subcortical nodules plus HuC/HuD or alpha-internexin with TUMOUR-CELL CD34 NEGATIVE.
Fibrillary astrocytoma: a histological subtype CNS5 no longer recognises. Code as documented; never assign prospectively.

morphology_entries.imaging_features: NF1 established on the Legius 2021 criteria, plus an MRI appearance typical of optic pathway glioma (fusiform enlargement of the optic nerve, chiasm or tracts) at C72.3. Atypical or unclear imaging goes to biopsy. Confidence stays below histologically confirmed: the consensus recommendation is evidence level III and no MRI-versus-histology accuracy figure exists in the evidence set (Revision 2 §3.5).
morphology_entries.coding_note: Pilocytic astrocytoma, /1 only, and the commonest paediatric CNS tumour in most series -- it exists in the registry only because site_profile.registry_policy.register_nonmalignant_cns is true (§1.3, §1.7). One of the two imaging-sufficient entries in the whole group, and the stronger of the two: Darrigo Junior 2025 recommendation 4 reached 100% first-round agreement that biopsy is not recommended for diagnostic confirmation of optic pathway glioma in NF1, with MRI the gold standard and the consensus explicitly endorsing MRI in resource-limited regions. Gated four ways (§3.5): NF1 established on the Legius 2021 criteria, imaging typical, confidence below histologically confirmed, and an NF1-screening flag so these cases can be analysed separately. Emit at C72.3 to match the ENCR Table 3 row. Registrability is live and unresolved: reported prevalence 15-30% across series and counting every imaging-detected lesion will inflate incidence materially; 8.9% is a five-year REGRESSION rate, not a prevalence -- do not use it as one. Two paediatric traps: 25% of paediatric spinal 'pilocytic astrocytomas' are actually DLGNT (Metais 2023), so a spinal piloid tumour must not default here and the discriminator is 1p deletion by FISH at RL IV; and the adult anaplastic-pilocytic-astrocytoma criteria do not apply to children (Gareton 2020, 77% of cases so labelled were plain pilocytic astrocytoma) -- delete that branch.

Polar spongioblastoma: one of the eight codes Revision 2 §1.6 records as having had no diagnostic content anywhere in the previous revision, and one of the six that remain legacy strings. Not a CNS5 entity. Code as documented; never assign prospectively.

Pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma. ICD-O-3.2 carries 'Anaplastic pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma' as a Related term, so the grade-3 call and the CDKN2A homozygous deletion behind it do not change the code -- code_neutral_molecular true. The code-identity trap: under ICD-O-3.2, 9424 (IIIb) and 9445 (IIId3) are different tumours, so this is no longer a dual-code problem -- but the PREVIOUS revision actively instructed coding PXA as 9445, and a legacy file coded 9445 for a PXA now reads as Glioblastoma, IDH-mutant. Historical 9445 entries at paediatric ages must be flagged for review, never migrated automatically (§1.5). '9445 - Pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma' in circulation belongs to this code and is an alias input.

Pilomyxoid astrocytoma. CNS5 treats the pilomyxoid appearance as a pattern of pilocytic astrocytoma; ICD-O-3.2 keeps the separate code at /3. Fallback is 9421/1 -- where pilomyxoid features are not established the tumour is a pilocytic astrocytoma, and the behaviour falls from /3 to /1. Revision 2 §1.3 trap 2 is explicit that traffic runs both ways and that a behaviour model which only ratchets upward will be wrong.

morphology_entries.iccc3_subgroup_name: Neuroepithelial glial tumors of uncertain origin
morphology_entries.coding_note: Astroblastoma. Wood 2018 reclassified most cases into other entities; CNS5 recognises 'Astroblastoma, MN1-altered', which is reachable only at RL V and shares this code, so the molecular finding is code-neutral. At RL I-IV emit 9430/3 with the Track B rendering 'tumour with astroblastic pattern'; the RL IV route is pseudorosettes WITH HYALINISATION plus MN1 break-apart FISH (38% or more of nuclei against about 9% in controls). Revision 2 names no IHC panel for it, so ihc_markers_required is null by decision, not omission. 9430/3 is a current ICD-O-3.2 code and is restored to the tree. IARC marks the TERM 'Astroblastoma' [obs]; it does not retire the number. Three checks, all within ICD-O-3.2: [obs] is term-level — 40 ICD-O-3.2 code/behaviour pairs carry [obs] and non-[obs] terms side by side; 9430 is absent from IARC's 'Deleted codes and their terms' (IACR, 9 October 2020), which is where a retired NUMBER is recorded; and the Belgian Cancer Registry's WHO CNS5 coding table assigns Astroblastoma, MN1-altered the ICD-O-3.2 code 9430/3, footnoted 'These entities have undergone a change in terminology of a previous code'. The obsolete wording stays off screen — the WHO CNS5 entity name is what the annotation carries. Registrar's ruling, 14 September 2026.
morphology_entries.obsolete_term_string_source: IARC ICD-O-3.2 morphology table (ICD-O-3.2_final_update09102020.xls, sha256 7ca51dcb...78a21), column 'obs' = [obs]. The marker is on the term, not on the code: the code is current and the tree emits it. The ICD-O-3.2 wording is not shown to the clerk; the WHO CNS5 entity name is.

morphology_entries.iccc3_subgroup_name: Neuroepithelial glial tumors of uncertain origin
morphology_entries.coding_note: Angiocentric glioma, /1 -- a registrability case under §1.3 and registrable because register_nonmalignant_cns is true. H&E perivascular bipolar pseudorosettes plus GFAP plus dot-like EMA; MYB::QKI is confirmatory (12/14) and is reachable by FISH, but the code is 9431/1 either way, so the molecular finding is code-neutral and the fallback rendering is 'Glioma with angiocentric pattern, NOS' at the same code (§4.3). It is a DIPG MIMIC with a median age of 5 years, and brainstem angiocentric glioma is one of the six diversion criteria that force the tissue branch away from the 9440/3 imaging endpoint (§3.5).

morphology_entries.nos_fallback_name: Neoplasm, uncertain whether benign or malignant
morphology_entries.coding_note: Neurohypophyseal, TTF-1 positive. CNS5 groups pituicytoma, granular cell tumour of the sellar region and spindle cell oncocytoma in one section but classifies them separately; ICCC-3 splits them too -- 9432/1 and 9582/0 are IIIe2, 8290/0 is IIIe1 (Revision 2 §4.12). Fallback is 8000/1 and not 9350/1: craniopharyngioma is a different entity, not a less specific one.

morphology_entries.imaging_features: Pons involved over at least 50% of its cross-section and the lesion centred in the pons; diffuse T2/FLAIR hyperintensity with ill-defined margins; minimal or no enhancement; symptom history under six months. Diversion to the tissue branch on any of: age under 3, history of 6 months or more, calcification, nodular enhancement, exophytic growth, angiocentric features (Revision 2 §3.5).
morphology_entries.coding_note: The high-grade glial hub, and the code CNS5's hardest nomenclature rule bites on: 'the term glioblastoma is no longer used in the setting of a pediatric-type neoplasm' -- the CODE is permissible, the DIAGNOSIS STRING is not, so the two-track output carries the descriptive diagnosis while this code is emitted. Under ruling 9 that warning lives in docs/clinical-warnings.md; clinical_alert is null. ICD-O-3.2 carries 'Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype', 'Diffuse midline glioma, NOS' and 'Diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma' as Related terms, so this is where an untested midline pontine tumour lands -- and where the subgroup-shift artefact of §1.5 originates: H3 K27M tested and positive gives 9385/3 in IIId2, untested gives 9440/3 in IIIb, the same tumour in a different ICCC-3 subgroup depending on one available immunostain. A site that acquires H3 K27M IHC mid-series will show IIIb falling and IIId2 rising and it will look epidemiological. The second of the two imaging-sufficient entries, and the weaker: Hankinson 2011 measured interobserver agreement among paediatric neurosurgeons at kappa 0.297, 0 of 16 tumours reaching unanimity, and concluded imaging-only diagnosis does not reach the threshold to be a standard of care -- so the DIPG endpoint is a flagged, lower-confidence, non-verified terminal, never the default, at ENCR basis 2 with no_tissue true and a non-empty diversion list. Biopsy is meanwhile demonstrably safe: Puget, 130 children, 100% yield, 0% mortality, 0% permanent morbidity, 3.9% transient. '9385 - Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype' in circulation belongs to this code (§1.1b). Paediatric mimics that must divert: brainstem angiocentric glioma (median age 5) and brainstem MYB/MYBL1-altered tumours.
Giant cell glioblastoma. Same CNS5 nomenclature rule as 9440/3: the code is permissible in a child, the diagnosis string is not.
Gliofibroma: not a CNS5 entity. Code as documented; never assign prospectively.

Gliosarcoma. The clinically natural fallback is 9440/3 Glioblastoma, NOS, but check_fallback_chains collapses the fallback graph to four-digit codes, so both behaviours of 9442 must target the same code or the collapsed edge is decided by array order. Both therefore point at 9400 Astrocytoma, NOS, which is correct if less specific: the astrocytic lineage survives, the grade does not.

morphology_entries.iccc3_subgroup_name: Neuroepithelial glial tumors of uncertain origin
morphology_entries.coding_note: Chordoid glioma; Related term 'Chordoid glioma of third ventricle'. /1, and registrable under §1.3.

morphology_entries.iccc3_subgroup_name: Neuroepithelial glial tumors of uncertain origin
morphology_entries.coding_note: NAMES AN ENTITY CNS5 ABOLISHED. Glioblastoma, IDH-mutant was deleted outright by CNS5; such tumours are Astrocytoma, IDH-mutant, CNS WHO grade 4. The code should essentially never be assigned to a new case and NEVER to a child (§1.2). Related term 'Glioblastoma, secondary, NOS'. The historical hazard is the sharper one: the PREVIOUS revision of this pathway actively instructed coding pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma as 9445, so a legacy file coded 9445 for a PXA now reads as Glioblastoma, IDH-mutant. Under ICD-O-3.2, 9424 (IIIb) and 9445 (IIId3) are different tumours in different subgroups, so this is no longer a dual-code problem -- historical 9445 entries at paediatric ages must be FLAGGED FOR REVIEW, never migrated automatically (§1.5). One of the 15 preferred terms not in circulation. Fallback 9440/3: with IDH untested the code is Glioblastoma, NOS.

The oligodendroglial hub. 9450/3 carries 'Oligodendroglioma, IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted' as a Related term, so the molecularly defined entity and the NOS entity share one code and the distinction is an annotation, not a code -- code_neutral_molecular true. Paediatric caveat the previous revision lacked: true IDH-mutant 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendroglioma is RARE IN CHILDREN, and an oligodendroglioma-like paediatric tumour is more likely PLNTY, DLGNT, DGONC, clear cell ependymoma or extraventricular neurocytoma -- route the differential accordingly rather than treating 9450 as the default for fried-egg cells. Where IDH and 1p/19q are both unavailable, which is the usual case, emit 9450/3 with provisional_pending naming both, confidence low, and the Track B rendering 'Oligodendroglioma, NOS'. Santosh's RL III surrogate route (HIP1R, vimentin, H3 K27me3) APPROXIMATES 1p/19q status but does not establish it, so it is not in the required marker set. Kurokawa's low-resource imaging rule -- 2 or more of subcortical FLAIR signal drop, multiple cystic/necrotic changes, calcification, using only T2, FLAIR and CT: sensitivity 48.0%, specificity 100% -- is adult-derived and ranks the differential only; imaging_sufficient is false.

The code exists; the CNS5 diagnosis does not. Related term 'Oligodendroglioma, anaplastic, IDH-mutant and 1p/19q codeleted' -- note ICD-O-3.2 writes 'codeleted' without a hyphen here while 9450/3 writes '1p/19q-codeleted' with one. One of the 15 preferred terms §1.1b records as not in circulation; the string '9451 - Oligodendroglioma, anaplastic' in circulation lacks the ', NOS' suffix and is an alias input only.
Oligodendroblastoma: obsolete. Code as documented and annotate; never assign prospectively (§4.8).
morphology_entries.obsolete_source: IARC ICD-O-3.2 morphology table (ICD-O-3.2_final_update09102020.xls, sha256 7ca51dcb...78a21), column 'obs' = [obs]. No non-obsolete term exists for this code at this behaviour. Removed from the decision tree by registrar's ruling, 2026-09-14; retained here so historical records and alias input still resolve.

morphology_entries.coding_note: Medulloblastoma, NOS -- the histologically defined diagnosis and the medulloblastoma family hub. Related terms: Classic medulloblastoma, Melanotic medulloblastoma. RL I-II output is H&E plus reticulin (which separates true desmoplastic/nodular from nodular classic) plus retained INI1; without IHC the rendered diagnosis is the descriptive 'CNS embryonal tumor, NOS', ADAPTR grade IV. Sarkar's own text and figure legends disagree about RL II -- §2.5.1 says the diagnosis can be confirmed at RL II while the Fig 1A and 1B legends both say a WHO CNS5 diagnosis cannot be determined at that level; reported, not resolved, and the conservative reading is that RL II confirms medulloblastoma but not a CNS5 molecular type. 'All medulloblastomas are grade 4' is NOT what CNS5 says: grade 4 is stated for SHH-activated and in the text for WNT-activated, no grade is mentioned for non-WNT/non-SHH, and CNS5 Table 3 lists no medulloblastoma at all. Emit an Arabic grade only where CNS5 states one; otherwise grade null on Track A or the ADAPTR Roman grade on Track B.

Desmoplastic nodular medulloblastoma, and -- via its Related terms -- the code an IHC-only site emits for SHH-activated medulloblastoma. Two Related strings are load-bearing and must be reproduced exactly: 'Medulloblastoma, SHH-activated and TP53-wildtype' and 'Medulloblastoma, SHH activated, NOS' -- note the ABSENCE of a hyphen in 'SHH activated' in the second, where the sibling term on the same code has one (contract §5.4). Panel and thresholds (Harry 2025, WHO-recommended cut-offs): GAB1 cytoplasmic 10% or more, YAP1 nuclear and/or cytoplasmic 10% or more, beta-catenin nuclear negative, INI1 retained. Harry reports NO accuracy, sensitivity, specificity or concordance for this panel -- 32 children, single centre, no molecular gold standard, validity claimed by citation only. p53 IHC cannot establish TP53 status and this is a hard stop (Orr 2020): two patterns, diffuse overexpression and complete absence from null variants, no definitive cut-off, and the >10% figure in circulation comes from infiltrating gliomas not medulloblastoma; Ranade found p53 indeterminate in 11-13% of SHH cases, 4 of them completely negative. So an IHC-only site emits 9471/3 and NEVER 9476/3; p53 IHC is a trigger for sequencing and genetic counselling, not a substitute. The YAP1 token here is the medulloblastoma molecular-group surrogate and is unrelated to the YAP1 ependymoma fusion partner of §4.1 -- do not collapse them.
Medullomyoblastoma: not a CNS5 entity. Code as documented; never assign prospectively.
morphology_entries.obsolete_source: IARC ICD-O-3.2 morphology table (ICD-O-3.2_final_update09102020.xls, sha256 7ca51dcb...78a21), column 'obs' = [obs]. No non-obsolete term exists for this code at this behaviour. Removed from the decision tree by registrar's ruling, 2026-09-14; retained here so historical records and alias input still resolve.

morphology_entries.coding_note: NOT a legacy bucket. 9473/3's ICD-O-3.2 preferred term is 'CNS embryonal tumor, NOS' and it is the LIVE NOS home for the entire new CNS embryonal family (§4.5). Everything below falls here when its defining test is unavailable, which for two of them is always in an RL I-IV setting: CNS neuroblastoma FOXR2-activated (RL V only, NGS; the only IHC route with performance data is SOX10 plus ANKRD55 TOGETHER -- sensitivity 100%, specificity 98%, Korshunov 84+263+9 tumours -- and it must be used only as a pair, because SOX10 alone is 92% sensitive but only 78% specific and is explicitly not sufficient to distinguish CNS neuroblastoma from midline glioblastoma, 25% of which stain in more than 75% of cells, while ANKRD55 stains 30% of ETMRs, the entity in the adjacent row of the same differential); CNS tumour with BCOR internal tandem duplication (RL IV, Sanger for the exon 15 ITD, frozen preferred -- focal/patchy OLIG2 is suggestive only and BCOR IHC misses some alterations); ETMR below RL IV; and CRINET (RL III: INI1 loss plus cribriform/trabecular growth plus EMA-positive cribriform surfaces plus no rhabdoid cells, 20% germline, and CNS5 assigns it NO grade). code_neutral_molecular is true because those entities are recorded as annotations against this one code. §4.7 is explicit that where INI1 is unavailable in an infant with a posterior fossa mass the honest output is 9473/3 with provisional_pending naming INI1 -- NOT 8000/3, which discards the embryonal morphology the pathologist did establish.
morphology_entries.topography_routing_note: IIIc2 at every site: ICCC-2017 range 29 is the only range carrying 9473, at sites 000-809. 9473/3 carries 'Central primitive neuroectodermal tumor' and 'Supratentorial PNET' as Related terms and 'Primitive neuroectodermal tumor, NOS' / 'PNET, NOS' / 'CPNET' as Synonyms. A peripheral PNET is not coded here: ICD-O-3.2 codes the peripheral wordings at 9364/3 Ewing sarcoma ('Peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor', 'PPNET'), Group VIII at bone and Group IX elsewhere. The router's former 9473 rule was removed on 2 October 2026 (Group 9 build contract §3.12).

morphology_entries.coding_note: Large cell medulloblastoma; Related term 'Anaplastic medulloblastoma'. LCA histology is one of Orr 2020's two triggers for germline testing in SHH medulloblastoma (the other is a mutant p53 pattern), recommended 'particularly in children (ages 3-18)' -- which, with the registry's upper age bound at 18, applies throughout (§1.7).

The spelling exemption this entry used to carry is retired. The 2019 draft workbook printed 'Medullobloastoma, WNT-activated, NOS'; IARC's final ICD-O-3.2 workbook (ICD-O-3.2_final_update09102020.xls, 9 October 2020) spells it correctly, so morphology_name now round-trips against the database with no exemption and no source_term anchor. The one quantified marker in the whole corpus is LEF1 (Ranade 2025, n=151 against a 12-gene RT-PCR / NanoString standard, 40 WNT / 45 SHH / 66 non-WNT-non-SHH): diffuse LEF1 at 50% or more of cells gives 100% PPV, 100% specificity, 80% sensitivity (32/40); ANY LEF1 positivity is 100% sensitive (40/40) but NOT specific, with focal positivity in 3/45 SHH cases (6.67%); all 66 non-WNT/non-SHH were negative. Branch rule: diffuse LEF1 50% or more gives WNT-activated here at high confidence; FOCAL LEF1 is not WNT on that evidence alone and must continue to GAB1/YAP1. Beta-catenin nuclear 15% or more is Harry's WHO-recommended cut-off; the 92.1% sensitivity at a 5% cut-off is cited by Ranade FROM Aboubakr 2024, a different cohort of 136 medulloblastomas with 38 WNT, not measured in Ranade's own series, and it conflicts with Harry's threshold -- record the cut-off used with every result and do not attribute the figure to Ranade. '9477 - Medulloblastoma, WNT-activated' in circulation is not an ICD-O-3.2 term and is an alias input pointing here.

THE ONLY GROUP III CODE ABSENT FROM THE REDCAP OPTION LIST, built anyway under ruling 3 and declaring awaiting_layer1 -- no other entry in this file carries that flag (contract §5.5). It also gets a row in docs/codes-awaiting-redcap.md. One of the two codes Revision 2 supplies diagnostic content for that the previous revision left blank (§1.6). RL V: TP53 SEQUENCING, not p53 IHC. Sarkar places it at RL III on the p53 IHC pattern and §4.4 sets that aside on the evidence -- Orr 2020 shows p53 IHC cannot establish TP53 status and cannot distinguish germline from somatic disruption. Never emit this code on IHC alone; the IHC-only destination is 9471/3, whose Related term is 'Medulloblastoma, SHH activated, NOS'. That is also why the fallback is 9471/3 rather than 9470/3: the SHH lineage is established by IHC, only the TP53 status is not. '9475 - Medulloblastoma, SHH-activated and TP53-mutant' in circulation belongs to this code and is an alias input.

awaiting_layer1.reason: 9476 Medulloblastoma, SHH-activated and TP53-mutant is absent from the REDCap `iii_morph` option list (verified against the live data dictionary export, 2026-09-14 — it is the only Group III code missing). Built anyway under registrar ruling 3 of 4 Sep 2026: the tree may run ahead of the dropdown so long as the two stay reconcilable in writing. ICD-O-3.2 carries the code and the term; ICCC-2017 places it in IIIc1.

morphology_entries.coding_note: THE code_neutral_molecular case for this group. Medulloblastoma group 3 versus group 4 needs DNA methylation profiling and IHC cannot distinguish them -- but BOTH are Related terms of 9477/3, so the distinction changes no code and the tool must not build the branch at all. Record it as unreachable, note it is code-neutral, and stop. Even with expression profiling Ranade left 11/151 (7%) as 'overlapping group 3/4'. Reached when beta-catenin, GAB1 and YAP1 are all negative with INI1 retained. The 14 molecular subgroups are RL V and also code-neutral. '9478 - Medulloblastoma, non-WNT/non-SHH' in circulation belongs to this code and is an alias input.

morphology_entries.morphology_name: Embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes with C19MC alteration
morphology_entries.coding_note: ETMR, AND IT SITS IN ICCC-3 SUBGROUP IIIc1 'MEDULLOBLASTOMAS'. An embryonal tumour with multilayered rosettes is not a medulloblastoma, so every ETMR the registry codes INFLATES the medulloblastoma subgroup. Flag it in the entity annotation and report IIIc1 with and without 9478 (§1.5, §4.4). RL IV: C19MC amplification by FISH in more than 10% of cells OVERRIDES histology; not possible at RL III. Order is INI1 first, then LIN28A at 25% or more cytoplasmic, then C19MC FISH; LIN28A-positive with C19MC-negative gives ETMR NEC or a DICER1-associated tumour, and DICER1 Sanger is the follow-on. NEVER let LIN28A alone make the call: Jakobiec 2015 found C19MC amplification in 0 of 20 intraocular medulloepitheliomas despite LIN28A positivity in 19 of 20 -- those are ciliary body, unilateral, DICER1-associated, and outside Group III entirely. diagnostic_tests_required names Cytogenetics/FISH; the DICER1 Sanger branch declares satisfies_tests rather than the entry adding Molecular/PCR, because the list has no OR semantics.

9480/3 carries two things at once. The ICD-O-3.2 term is 'Cerebellar sarcoma, NOS', which IARC marks [obs] and which is a legacy string, and the code is also where WHO CNS5's Primary intracranial sarcoma, DICER1-mutant lands - the Belgian Cancer Registry's CNS5 coding table assigns it 9480/3 under the footnote 'These entities have undergone a change in terminology of a previous code'. The ceiling is therefore high, not low: a DICER1-confirmed case is established, and the legacy-string branch reaches its own low confidence on the branch. ICCC-3 files 9480 in IIIc1 with the medulloblastomas at any topography, which is why the fallback stays inside that family rather than leaving for IIIf. Note 'Circumscribed arachnoidal cerebellar sarcoma' is a SYNONYM of 9471/3, not of this code.

morphology_entries.coding_note: Gangliocytoma, NOS -- the /0 neuronal hub for this subgroup. '9492 - Gangliocytoma' without the ', NOS' suffix is in circulation, is not an ICD-O-3.2 term and is an alias input only (§1.1b). Revision 2 names no gangliocytoma-specific panel, so ihc_markers_required is null by decision, not omission.

Dysplastic gangliocytoma of cerebellum (Lhermitte-Duclos). Imaging is in the required set because the 'tiger-striped' MRI appearance is part of the diagnosis (§4.14). The PTEN / Cowden syndrome referral flag is a germline finding that changes no code -- code_neutral_molecular true -- and under ruling 9 the warning itself lives in docs/clinical-warnings.md.

Medulloepithelioma has no place in WHO CNS5 -- it is not a CNS5 CNS tumour type -- but remains in ICD-O-3.2 and in ICCC-3, topography-gated to C70.0-C72.9. Code as documented in the file and annotate 'not a WHO CNS5 type'. Do NOT assign prospectively to a tumour that meets ETMR criteria: that is 9478/3. The fallback leaves the subgroup for IIIf rather than joining the embryonal family at 9473/3, because §4.6 puts these codes outside CNS5 altogether and because both behaviours of 9501 must target one code for check_fallback_chains, which collapses the graph to four digits.
morphology_entries.topography_routing_note: ICCC-3 gates 9501-9504 to C70.0-C72.9. Outside that range these codes leave Group III and route to Group IV by ICCC-3's own ranges; an intraocular medulloepithelioma at C69.4 is outside Group III entirely. Revision 2 §4.5: Jakobiec 2015 found C19MC amplification in 0 of 20 intraocular medulloepitheliomas despite LIN28A positivity in 19 of 20, so an intraocular case is neither Group III nor ETMR (Revision 2 §4.6).

morphology_entries.nos_fallback_name: Neoplasm, uncertain whether benign or malignant
morphology_entries.coding_note: Ganglioglioma, NOS -- the /1 glioneuronal hub, and with DNET one of the two commonest tumours in paediatric drug-resistant epilepsy surgery series. CD34 positivity in the cortical GFAP-positive cells is the supporting finding; BRAF V600E is present in about 60% of gangliogliomas and changes no code, so code_neutral_molecular is true. Several CNS5 entities with no ICD-O-3.2 code fall here or to 9509/1 by morphology, or to 8000/1: myxoid glioneuronal tumour (PDGFRA p.Lys385Leu/Ile, a single-exon Sanger target and therefore RL IV-reachable and cheap), DLGNT (oligodendroglioma-like plus Olig2 plus a neuronal marker plus 1p deletion plus a MAPK alteration) and DGONC (a PROVISIONAL type -- carry provisional true, never the string '(provisional type)', which is an extraction artefact of the source's italics). DLGNT matters most operationally: 25% of paediatric spinal 'pilocytic astrocytomas' are actually DLGNT (§4.3).

Anaplastic ganglioglioma. Cannot fall back to 9505/1 -- check_fallback_chains keys the graph by morphology_code alone and a within-code hop reads as a self-reference -- and ICD-O-3.2 has no malignant glioneuronal NOS code, so the chain leaves for IIIf at 8000/3, which keeps both behaviours of 9505 pointing at one target code.

morphology_entries.nos_fallback_name: Neoplasm, uncertain whether benign or malignant
morphology_entries.coding_note: Central neurocytoma; Related terms 'Cerebellar liponeurocytoma' and 'Extraventricular neurocytoma', so all three share this code. Extraventricular neurocytoma is one of the entities that should be considered before 9450/3 for an oligodendroglioma-like paediatric tumour (§4.8). '9506 - Neurocytoma' in circulation is not an ICD-O-3.2 term and is an alias input only.
Pacinian tumour: a legacy string with no CNS diagnostic content. Code as documented; never assign prospectively.

Atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumour, reachable at RL III, and Sarkar says referral beyond it is generally unnecessary -- 'practically all cases can be given a WHO CNS5 diagnosis at RL III'. INI1/SMARCB1 IHC WITH AN INTACT INTERNAL CONTROL identifies more than 95%; the marker is an EXCLUDE here because it is the LOSS of INI1 that defines the tumour. Where INI1 is RETAINED, test BRG1/SMARCA4 (0.5-2% of cases) -- Sarkar's Table 6 says to check BRG1 when INI-1 is negative, the body text says when INI1 is retained, and §4.7 rules that the BODY TEXT is implemented and the table entry is an error. INI1 loss is NOT specific: it also occurs in CRINET, in desmoplastic myxoid tumour of the pineal region and in poorly differentiated chordoma, so the branch must adjudicate rather than terminate. The germline implication (rhabdoid tumour predisposition syndrome) is code-neutral and, under ruling 9, lives in docs/clinical-warnings.md. Any infant under 3 with a posterior fossa mass needs SMARCB1 IHC before a medulloblastoma code is assigned; where INI1 is unavailable the output is 9473/3 with provisional_pending, not 8000/3.

Papillary glioneuronal tumour; Related term 'Rosette-forming glioneuronal tumor', so both share this code. Revision 2 names no panel specific to it, so ihc_markers_required is null by decision rather than an invented glial/neuronal pair. With 9505/1 it is one of the two morphological destinations for the codeless CNS5 glioneuronal entities (§4.14).

The meningioma hub. Related terms: lymphoplasmacyte-rich, metaplastic, microcystic and secretory meningioma. THE PAEDIATRIC RULING (§1.7, §4.15): with the registry's upper age bound at 18, EVERY meningioma in this registry falls inside Berghaus 2026's 0-21 band, where WHO grade, methylation class, UCSF class and the integrated risk score ALL FAIL to stratify progression-free survival, and where CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion and TERT promoter mutations were ENTIRELY ABSENT (the only cases were aged 33, 36 and 38). So the cIMPACT-NOW update 8 molecular grading rules are NOT the default path here -- they stay in the tree marked evidence_population adult, and update 8 itself excludes paediatric, radiation-associated and NF2 meningiomas from its evidence base. The default is Berghaus's hierarchy: EXTENT OF RESECTION FIRST (dominant predictor, highest c-index), then SMARCE1 / BAP1 / NF2, then 17q. SMARCE1-altered is intermediate risk of recurrence and BAP1-altered is high risk -- stated as RISK TIERS, not grades; the grade equivalences Berghaus mentions are cited to Sievers et al., a paper not held in this library, and BAP1 alterations occurred in 0.6% of the 0-21 group (about one patient), so treat the BAP1 branch as provisional. Those findings change no code, hence code_neutral_molecular true. The paediatric tumour is a different tumour: F:M 0.9, clear cell 15.2% versus 1.4% over 39, spinal 13.4%, gain-dominated copy number with chr17q gain, 1p loss carrying NO prognostic weight, SMARCE1 altered in 13.7%, NF2 in 37.3%. Update 8's own rule also lands here: a brain-invasive otherwise-benign meningioma with no genetic testing should be termed 'meningioma, NOS' WITH THE GRADE OMITTED -- grade_resolution.unresolved must never invent one.

Meningioma, malignant -- the code for CNS WHO grade 3. H&E route: 20 or more mitoses in 10 HPF of 0.16 mm-squared, equivalently 12.5 or more per mm-squared (the grade-2 threshold is 4 and 2.5). Record the unit; a band list without a denominator is a build error (contract §2(7)). Tier 1 FISH route: CDKN2A/B HOMOZYGOUS deletion gives grade 3 -- hemizygous deletion is explicitly insufficient, as is H3K27me3. TERT promoter mutation gives grade 3 at tier 2. Two things that must not be built: do not branch on 1q gain (Landry 2025 proposes it explicitly for 'the next iteration' of WHO grading on n=7 grade-1 patients at risk, and it is in none of the descriptions of update 8 in this corpus); and do not let FISH carry the 1p/22q rules (Crumley 2026 versus CMA: 1p 45.83% agreement kappa 0.16, 22q 62.50% kappa 0.21, on per-arm denominators of 11 and 24, not 113 -- and CDKN2A showed 96.43% agreement with kappa 0.00, the agreement entirely shared negativity since CMA found 0/70. 3 of 12 update-8 upgrades in that series rested on FISH calls contradicted by both CMA and WES). Any arm-level 1p/22q call made by FISH carries a low-confidence flag. Masui's dissent is logged as the minority view: most institutions in LMICs lack easy access to molecular diagnostics, so the feasibility of applying costly genetic testing to common operable meningiomas needs validation. Follow Landry and update 8; log Masui. All of it is evidence_population adult.

Meningothelial meningioma, /0 only. Interobserver agreement on meningioma subtype is poor (Rogers 2016), which is why the subtype codes cap at medium and why §4.15 moves the clear cell call off H&E and onto SMARCE1.
Fibrous meningioma, /0 only. See 9531/0.
Psammomatous meningioma, /0 only. See 9531/0.
Angiomatous meningioma, /0 only. See 9531/0.

Haemangioblastic meningioma. IARC marks both ICD-O-3.2 terms on this code [obs] — 'Hemangioblastic meningioma' and its synonym 'Angioblastic meningioma' — and the entity they named is not a meningioma at all. It is meningeal haemangiopericytoma, a term WHO CNS5 retires in favour of solitary fibrous tumour (Louis DN, et al. Neuro-Oncology 2021;23(8):1231–1251, p. 1248), which is 8815 in ICD-O-3.2 and ICCC-3 IXb1 — Group IX. A true haemangioblastoma is 9161, ICCC-3 IXd8 — also Group IX. The decision tree therefore refers such a report to Group IX and emits no Group III code. Retained here so a historical record coded 9535/0 still resolves; never assign prospectively.
morphology_entries.obsolete_source: IARC ICD-O-3.2 morphology table (ICD-O-3.2_final_update09102020.xls, sha256 7ca51dcb...78a21), column 'obs' = [obs]. No non-obsolete term exists for this code at this behaviour. Removed from the decision tree by registrar's ruling, 2026-09-14; retained here so historical records and alias input still resolve.

morphology_entries.coding_note: Transitional meningioma, /0 only. See 9531/0.

Clear cell meningioma; Related term 'Chordoid meningioma' -- both are CNS WHO grade 2 BY SUBTYPE and both share this code. SMARCE1 is bidirectional and quantified: loss in 12/12 clear cell meningiomas, retained in 320/320 controls (305 meningiomas of other subtypes plus 15 clear cell mimics including 4 clear cell ependymomas), kappa 1.00 against sequencing, reachable at RL III. The marker is an EXCLUDE because it is the LOSS that defines the tumour. §4.15 rules the branch must be GATED ON SMARCE1, NOT ON H&E: Rogers 2016 gives clear cell meningioma near-worst interobserver agreement in the group (focal kappa 0.17, just above papillary at 0.16; for diffuse clear cell there was no agreement at all, though on only 3 cases, 1.4%). Clear cell is 15.2% of paediatric meningiomas against 1.4% over 39, so this branch fires far more often here than the adult literature implies.

Papillary meningioma; Related term 'Rhabdoid meningioma'. §4.15: RHABDOID AND PAPILLARY ARE NO LONGER AUTOMATICALLY GRADE 3 -- the pattern alone does not carry the grade, and papillary has the worst interobserver agreement in the group (kappa 0.16, Rogers 2016). The /3 behaviour must rest on the grade-3 criteria of 9530/3, not on the architecture. Fallback 9530/3 keeps the behaviour; 9538/1 falls to 9530/0 for the same reason, so both behaviours of 9538 target code 9530.

Atypical meningioma. BRAIN INVASION ALONE NO LONGER YIELDS GRADE 2: update 8 rules that a brain-invasive otherwise-benign meningioma with no genetic testing should be termed 'meningioma, NOS' with the GRADE OMITTED, which is why the fallback is 9530/0 and why grade_resolution.unresolved must carry grade null with a reason rather than a number. The H&E threshold is 4 or more mitoses in 10 HPF of 0.16 mm-squared (2.5 or more per mm-squared); record the unit. Update 8's tier-2 rule -- grade 1 morphology plus 1p deletion (complete or segmental, more than 5% of the arm) plus 22q loss and/or an NF2 variant -- is evidence_population adult and is not the default path here (§1.7, §4.15). Molecular testing DOWNGRADES in meningioma as often as it upgrades: Masui 2026 found 1p loss in only 7 of 19 histological grade 2 meningiomas (37%), making 63% downgrade candidates.

Meningeal sarcomatosis: a legacy string, not a CNS5 entity. Code as documented; never assign prospectively. Diagnostic trap for any spindled or papillary meningeal tumour: TTF-1 is aberrantly expressed in meningeal solitary fibrous tumour and it is CLONE-DEPENDENT -- 34.3% with SPT24 but only 2 of 23 with 8G7D3/1 (Wu 2021) -- so a TTF-1-positive meningeal tumour can be mistaken for a metastasis and routed out of Group III entirely. Record the antibody clone.

morphology_entries.morphology_name: Granular cell tumor of sellar region
morphology_entries.coding_note: Neurohypophyseal, TTF-1 positive. See 9432/1 for the three-member family and why the fallback leaves the subgroup rather than passing through craniopharyngioma.

decision_trees.tree_label: Posterior fossa — cerebellum, fourth ventricle and brain stem (C71.6, C71.7)

nodes.question: Posterior fossa mass (cerebellum C71.6 or brain stem C71.7). What is actually in this patient's file, and was the specimen adequate for diagnosis?
nodes.hint: Pick the highest evidence tier present. Posterior fossa resection is often the only tissue that will ever exist, so record adequacy honestly: an uninterpretable specimen is not a negative one, and it must not be coded as though a diagnosis was reached.
nodes.coding_note: ENCR basis of diagnosis is computed from this gate as the highest of codes 1-8 (0 and 9 override). The two gaps ENCR leaves are declared on the tree object: ihc_counts_as 7, methylation_counts_as 8 (Revision 2 §2.6). No Group III terminal may emit basis 1 — every CNS row in ENCR Table 3 is basis 2. `ihc_tier` is the tree's own routing variable; it is NOT the engine's site resource level, which belongs to site_profile and is read per tumour family.

options.label: Referral letter or clinical note only — no imaging report and no pathology report
Imaging report only (MRI / CT) — no tissue and no cytology
options.coding_note: Imaging does three different jobs here: it fixes topography, it ranks the differential, and for exactly one entity in this compartment it is proposed as a diagnostic endpoint. Only the third is a terminal, and it is gated.

options.label: Intraoperative frozen section or squash cytology only — no definitive histology report has followed
options.coding_note: Jain 2022, paediatric CNS: frozen section sensitivity 91.43%, squash cytology 88.57%, kappa 0.729. An intraoperative diagnosis is never the coded diagnosis while definitive histology is still expected.

options.label: Definitive histology report — H&E, reticulin, PAS or Alcian blue only; no immunohistochemistry
options.coding_note: Resource level I. Reticulin is the stain that separates a true desmoplastic/nodular medulloblastoma from nodular classic morphology, and it is available at RL I.

options.label: Histology WITH basic diagnostic immunohistochemistry — GFAP, synaptophysin, EMA, S100, Ki-67, SMARCB1 (INI1)
options.coding_note: Resource level II. Basic IHC establishes lineage; it does not approximate a molecular result.

options.label: Histology WITH surrogate molecular immunohistochemistry — H3 K27me3, H3 K27M, EZHIP, LEF1, β-catenin, GAB1, YAP1, LIN28A, BRG1/SMARCA4
options.coding_note: Resource level III. This is the tier at which the medulloblastoma molecular axis, PFA ependymoma and AT/RT all become reachable.

options.label: Histology and IHC PLUS molecular testing — FISH, RT-PCR, Sanger or NGS sequencing, or DNA methylation profiling
options.coding_note: Resource level IV-V. Tick methylation only where a methylation class was actually reported; it is the one result that counts as ENCR basis 8 in its own right.

options.label: A specimen was taken but the report says it is inadequate, non-diagnostic, or crush artefact only
options.coding_note: Inadequate resolves to the group NOS code with a provisional pending re-biopsy, and to ENCR basis 2, not 7 — the tissue did not yield a diagnosis (Revision 2 §3.3).

options.label: The specimen could not be interpreted at all — stain failure, no residual lesional tissue on the levels cut
options.coding_note: Not assessable is not negative and is not inadequate-by-sampling. It routes to the same repeat-or-escalate node but must carry its own state so the clerk can see that a repeat is owed.

options.label: The posterior fossa is not established as the site — the lesion crosses compartments, or the site is not stated
Reviewed and NOT a neoplasm — cerebellar abscess, tuberculoma, demyelination or another non-neoplastic mass
options.reason: The lesion was reviewed and is not a neoplasm. In a high-TB, high-HIV setting a posterior fossa abscess, tuberculoma or a demyelinating pseudotumour is a real and recurring cause of a cerebellar mass. No morphology code is emitted and the case leaves the registry. This exit is for the genuinely non-neoplastic only: a benign or uncertain-behaviour CNS neoplasm IS registrable under the 14 September 2026 ruling and must be coded, not excluded.

nodes.question: What exactly does the referral or clinical note say?
nodes.hint: Nothing above 'a neoplasm of the posterior fossa' is reachable from a referral. Do not read medulloblastoma, ependymoma or pilocytic astrocytoma out of a clinical note — those three are the posterior fossa differential, and the letter naming one of them is not evidence that it is that one.
nodes.coding_note: 8000 is authored at /0, /1 and /3 only. /6 and /9 fall outside the group's 0-1,3 declaration and a case carrying them leaves Group III silently; metastatic disease is coded to the primary at Stage 1.

options.label: The note says a malignant brain tumour / posterior fossa tumour, and describes a CT or MRI that was done

diagnosis_rendering.comment: A referral naming a malignant posterior fossa tumour, with imaging performed and no pathology in the file. No morphological family is established, so no ADAPTR histologic grade can be assigned.

options.upgrade_path: Histology would place the case in a morphological family and give a family NOS code; basic IHC would separate embryonal, ependymal and glial lineage.

options.label: The note names a specific tumour — medulloblastoma, ependymoma, astrocytoma — but there is no pathology report in the file

diagnosis_rendering.comment: The referral names an entity. It is recorded verbatim on the case, but it is not coded: the posterior fossa differential is exactly the set of tumours a referral letter guesses between.

options.upgrade_path: The pathology report would settle this. Record the referral wording verbatim so the case can be re-coded when it arrives.
options.coding_note: Do not code the named entity. 8000/3 is the honest ceiling from a referral.

options.label: The note describes a lesion whose behaviour is not stated — a cerebellar mass under observation, no treatment decision recorded

diagnosis_rendering.descriptive_diagnosis: Neoplasm, uncertain whether benign or malignant
diagnosis_rendering.comment: Behaviour is not stated anywhere in the file and nothing in the record establishes it. Non-malignant CNS neoplasms are registrable, so /1 is a real answer here rather than a placeholder.

options.upgrade_path: Imaging or histology would establish behaviour.

options.label: The note describes a benign cerebellar neoplasm already treated and discharged, with no pathology report retrievable

diagnosis_rendering.comment: A benign CNS neoplasm is registrable under the 14 September 2026 ruling. It is coded at /0 rather than excluded.

options.upgrade_path: The operative pathology report would give the morphological family.

options.label: The note says only 'posterior fossa mass for investigation' — no diagnosis is asserted
options.coding_note: No malignancy has been asserted. This must go through the imaging gate before any code is considered.

nodes.question: No tissue exists. Tick every imaging feature the report actually states, then answer the marker questions and the tissue-diversion list below.
nodes.hint: Only one entity in this compartment has an imaging-only endpoint, and it is a flagged, lower-confidence, non-verified terminal — never the default. Interobserver agreement between paediatric neurosurgeons on the imaging diagnosis of DIPG was kappa 0.297 ('only fair'), 0 of 16 tumours reached unanimity, and the authors concluded that imaging-only diagnosis does not reach the threshold to be a standard of care. Biopsy in expert hands gave 100% yield and 0% mortality in 130 children. Everything else on this screen needs tissue.
nodes.coding_note: ENCR Table 3 permits registration on imaging for several CNS rows, all at basis 2. That is a registration permission, not a licence to assign the morphology code with high confidence — the two are separate fields and stay separate (Revision 2 §2.6, §3.5).
imaging_features: Tumour is centred in the pons
50% or more of the pons is involved on axial T2/FLAIR
Diffuse T2/FLAIR hyperintensity with ill-defined, infiltrative margins
Minimal or no contrast enhancement
Clinical picture is the DIPG triad — cranial neuropathy, long-tract signs, ataxia
History is under six months (COG criterion)
Cerebellar or fourth-ventricular mass, not brainstem
Midline mass with CSF or serum tumour markers requested

biochemical_questions.question: Serum AFP 25 ng/mL or above, or CSF β-hCG 8.2 IU/L or above — record the number, not a yes/no
Both AFP and β-hCG measured and both below those cut-offs

diversion_criteria.feature: Age under 3 years
diversion_criteria.reason: Favours an infant-type or embryonal tumour. Tissue is required.

diversion_criteria.feature: Symptom duration of 6 months or more
diversion_criteria.reason: Atypical for DIPG; consider brainstem angiocentric glioma or a MYB/MYBL1-altered tumour. Inclusion requires a history under 6 months, so the two rules meet with no gap.

diversion_criteria.feature: Calcification
diversion_criteria.reason: Atypical for DIPG.

diversion_criteria.feature: Nodular or ring enhancement
diversion_criteria.reason: Atypical for DIPG.

diversion_criteria.feature: Exophytic growth
diversion_criteria.reason: Favours a low-grade brainstem glioma.

diversion_criteria.feature: Angiocentric or perivascular growth pattern reported
diversion_criteria.reason: Brainstem angiocentric glioma (median age 5) and MYB/MYBL1-altered tumours both mimic diffuse midline glioma.

options.label: A midline mass with an ELEVATED serum AFP or CSF β-hCG
options.reason: An elevated AFP or β-hCG in a midline intracranial mass is a secreting germ cell tumour. It belongs in ICCC-3 Group X (germ cell, trophoblastic tumours and neoplasms of gonads), not Group III. Code it there and stop. nodes.question: Where inside the posterior fossa is the tumour centred?
nodes.hint: Compartment is asked before morphology because this group is classified by compartment first: CNS5 defines ependymoma by anatomical compartment, and the paediatric posterior fossa differential is a compartment differential before it is a histological one. The router already captured C71.6 or C71.7 — this question refines within it and asks the clerk nothing the file does not state.
nodes.coding_note: Subsite changes the prior, never the code. A midline fourth-ventricular mass in a child is medulloblastoma, ependymoma or AT/RT; a lateral cerebellar cyst with a mural nodule is pilocytic astrocytoma; a diffuse pons is a diffuse midline glioma. The codes reachable from each are identical — only the order of the questions changes.

options.site: Midline — fourth ventricle, vermis or the roof of the fourth ventricle (C71.6)
Cerebellopontine angle, or extending through the foramen of Luschka (C71.6)
options.coding_note: Lateral extension through the foramen of Luschka is the classic posterior fossa ependymoma habit, but it is a prior, not a diagnosis.

options.site: Brain stem — diffuse, centred in the pons (C71.7)
Brain stem — focal, exophytic, tectal or medullary (C71.7)
options.coding_note: A focal or exophytic brainstem tumour is more often a pilocytic astrocytoma or a low-grade glioma than a diffuse midline glioma.

options.site: Cerebellum, subsite within the posterior fossa not stated in the file
The tumour crosses out of the posterior fossa, or the site cannot be established from the file
options.coding_note: Site is a classification axis in this group, not a descriptor. Where it is not established the case belongs in the unspecified tree.

nodes.question: What morphological family does the H&E place this tumour in?
nodes.hint: Family first, entity second. At resource level I the tool's job is to place the case in a family and give the family's NOS code — not to guess a molecular type.
nodes.coding_note: Compartment has been fixed; this is the second axis. Molecular group, where it is reachable at all, is the third and is asked inside the family branch.

options.descriptor: Embryonal — densely cellular small round blue cells, high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, moulded nuclei, Homer Wright rosettes, brisk mitoses and apoptosis
options.coding_note: Every embryonal-morphology tumour in this compartment goes through SMARCB1 (INI1) before any medulloblastoma code is considered.

options.descriptor: Rhabdoid cells — eccentric nuclei, prominent nucleoli, eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions, with or without an embryonal background
options.coding_note: Rhabdoid morphology is suggestive of AT/RT but is neither necessary nor sufficient: many AT/RTs have no rhabdoid cells, and rhabdoid cells occur in other tumours. SMARCB1 (INI1) decides.

options.descriptor: Ependymal — perivascular pseudorosettes, monomorphic round nuclei, dot-like or ring EMA, fibrillary processes
Piloid / circumscribed astrocytic — biphasic compact and loose architecture, Rosenthal fibres, eosinophilic granular bodies, a cyst with an enhancing mural nodule
Diffusely infiltrating glial — tumour cells permeating parenchyma with no border, entrapped neurons or axons
Papillary / epithelial — delicate fibrovascular cores covered by a single layer of cuboidal-to-columnar epithelium, in or adjacent to the fourth ventricle
Neuronal or glioneuronal — ganglion cells, dysplastic cerebellar cortex with enlarged granular-layer neurons, or a uniform neurocytic population
Mesenchymal / sarcomatoid - spindle, pleomorphic or rhabdoid cells with no glial or neuronal differentiation; GFAP and OLIG2 negative where stained
options.coding_note: Added 2026-09-15. Routes to the shared node st_dicer1_sarcoma. Primary intracranial sarcoma, DICER1-mutant is 92% supratentorial with a median age of 6 years, so every compartment that can carry it reaches the node; g3_midline deliberately does not.

options.descriptor: Lymphoid — sheets of atypical lymphoid cells, angiocentric, CD20 or CD3 positive
options.reason: A primary CNS lymphoma belongs in ICCC-3 Group II (lymphomas and reticuloendothelial neoplasms), not Group III. Code it from the Group II tree; the intracranial site does not move it into this group.

options.descriptor: Germ cell — germinomatous sheets with lymphocytic infiltrate, yolk sac, teratomatous or choriocarcinomatous elements, or the file records an elevated AFP or β-hCG
options.reason: An intracranial germ cell tumour belongs in ICCC-3 Group X. Code it there. An elevated serum AFP (25 ng/mL or above) or CSF β-hCG (8.2 IU/L or above) routes out and stops; a normal result excludes nothing and the case proceeds to tissue, because marker-negative intracranial germ cell tumours are well documented. Record the numbers, not a yes/no.

nodes.question: SMARCB1 (INI1) immunohistochemistry — was it performed on this tumour, and what did it show?
nodes.hint: Any child under 3 with a posterior fossa mass needs SMARCB1 (INI1) before a medulloblastoma code is assigned. Atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumour is routinely misdiagnosed as medulloblastoma on imaging and H&E alone, and INI1 with an intact internal control identifies more than 95% of them. Where INI1 is RETAINED and the tumour still looks rhabdoid, BRG1/SMARCA4 is the next stain — it accounts for 0.5-2% of cases. Loss of either implies rhabdoid tumour predisposition syndrome and the family needs a genetics referral.
nodes.coding_note: Sarkar's Table 6 says to check BRG1 when 'INI-1 is negative'; the body text says when INI1 is RETAINED. The body text is implemented here — the table entry is an error, and implementing it would send every INI1-deficient tumour for a second stain it does not need while missing the 0.5-2% the stain exists to catch.

unreachable_destination.reason: SMARCB1 (INI1) immunohistochemistry is not available at this laboratory. The honest output is CNS embryonal tumor, NOS with INI1 named as the pending test — not 8000/3, which would discard the embryonal morphology the pathologist did establish.

nodes.question: SMARCB1 (INI1) is lost. Which of these does the rest of the material show?

nodes.question: C19MC amplification by FISH — what was done and what did it show?
nodes.hint: C19MC amplification, present in more than 10% of nuclei, OVERRIDES the histology: a tumour with C19MC amplification is an embryonal tumour with multilayered rosettes whatever the rosettes look like. The immunohistochemical route runs SMARCB1 (INI1) first, then LIN28A at 25% or more cytoplasmic, then C19MC FISH — and LIN28A alone never makes the call.
nodes.coding_note: 9478/3 sits in ICCC-3 subgroup IIIc1, 'Medulloblastomas'. An embryonal tumour with multilayered rosettes is not a medulloblastoma, so every ETMR the registry codes inflates the medulloblastoma subgroup. Report IIIc1 with and without 9478.

Evidence recorded there was: C19MC amplification demonstrated by FISH in more than 10% of nuclei. This finding overrides the histology.

nodes.question: A papillary tumour in or beside the fourth ventricle. Which stains were done and what did they show?

decision_trees.tree_label: Supratentorial compartment — cerebral hemispheres and lateral/third ventricles (C71.0–C71.5, C71.8)

nodes.question: What is in this patient's file for this supratentorial lesion, and was the specimen adequate for diagnosis?
nodes.hint: Pick the HIGHEST evidence tier that is actually in the file, not the one that was requested. A crush-artefact or non-diagnostic biopsy is INADEQUATE — it is not a negative biopsy, and it must not be recorded as one. An intraoperative frozen section or squash is never the coded diagnosis on its own.
nodes.coding_note: Router handoff for C71.0 Cerebrum, C71.1 Frontal lobe, C71.2 Temporal lobe, C71.3 Parietal lobe, C71.4 Occipital lobe, C71.5 Ventricle NOS and C71.8 Overlapping lesion of brain. C71.0 also carries thalamus and basal ganglia, so a thalamic diffuse midline glioma arrives in this tree. Resource level is computed PER TUMOUR FAMILY from site_profile, never as one number for the site (Revision 2 §2.2 rule 1) — the evidence tier captured here is the file's, not the laboratory's.

options.label: Referral letter or clinical note only — no pathology report and no imaging report in the file
Imaging report only — no tissue has been taken, or none will be

options.label: Intraoperative frozen section or squash cytology only — no definitive paraffin histology report

options.label: Definitive histology report (H&E) — no immunohistochemistry
Histology with basic diagnostic immunohistochemistry (GFAP, synaptophysin, EMA, Olig2, S100, Ki-67, INI1)

Histology plus a molecular result — FISH, RT-PCR, Sanger sequencing or MLPA
Histology plus DNA methylation profiling or NGS
The pathology report is in the file but hedges throughout ('suggestive of', 'cannot exclude') and never states whether the specimen was adequate

nodes.step_label: Is this a neoplasm at all?
nodes.question: The lesion has been reviewed and a non-neoplastic process is in question. What did the review establish?
nodes.hint: This exit is for the genuinely NON-NEOPLASTIC only. Benign is NOT a reason to use it: this registry registers non-malignant CNS neoplasms, so a pilocytic astrocytoma, a DNET, a ganglioglioma or a choroid plexus papilloma is registered at its own /0 or /1 code and must never be sent here.
