options.descriptor: Cerebral abscess — pus, neutrophils, a capsule, or organisms cultured
options.reason: A cerebral abscess is not a neoplasm. No morphology code is emitted and the case leaves the cancer registry.

options.descriptor: Tuberculoma — caseating granulomas, Langhans giant cells, or acid-fast bacilli
options.reason: A tuberculoma is not a neoplasm. In a high-TB setting this is a common supratentorial mass mimic. No morphology code is emitted.

options.descriptor: Tumefactive demyelination — macrophage-rich, myelin loss with relative axonal preservation
options.reason: Demyelination is not a neoplasm. It is a well documented mimic of a diffuse glioma, on imaging and on a small biopsy. No morphology code is emitted.

options.descriptor: Focal cortical dysplasia — dysmorphic neurons or balloon cells with no neoplastic population
options.reason: Focal cortical dysplasia is a malformation of cortical development, not a neoplasm. It is the commonest non-neoplastic finding in a paediatric epilepsy resection and must not be coded as a glioneuronal tumour. No morphology code is emitted.

options.descriptor: Gliosis, infarct, vascular malformation or another reactive process with no neoplastic population
options.reason: A reactive or vascular lesion is not a neoplasm. No morphology code is emitted and the case leaves the cancer registry.

options.descriptor: On review a neoplasm IS present after all

nodes.question: What morphological family does the H&E place this supratentorial tumour in?
nodes.hint: At RL I the job is the FAMILY, not the molecular type. Pick what the slide shows. Diffuse means the tumour infiltrates between normal neurones and glia with no border; circumscribed means it pushes against the brain with one.
nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 §3.6 and §6.3. Compartment was fixed by the router from the topography captured at Stage 1 (C71.0-C71.5, C71.8); this node is the morphological fork inside it. C71.0 carries thalamus and basal ganglia, so a thalamic diffuse midline glioma reaches the diffuse branch here.

options.descriptor: DIFFUSE glial tumour — infiltrates brain with no discrete border; astrocytic, oligodendroglial or mixed cytology
CIRCUMSCRIBED glial tumour — compact, pushing border; piloid, pleomorphic/xanthomatous, giant-cell, chordoid or astroblastic
GLIONEURONAL or NEURONAL tumour — ganglion cells, floating neurones, a specific glioneuronal element, vacuolated nodules, or a uniform neurocytic population
EPENDYMAL morphology — perivascular pseudorosettes, ependymal canals or rosettes, monomorphic nuclei
PAPILLARY intraventricular tumour of choroid plexus type — fibrovascular fronds covered by a single layer of cuboidal or columnar epithelium
EMBRYONAL — densely cellular small round blue cells, high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, brisk mitoses, with or without rosettes or rhabdoid cells
Dense LYMPHOID infiltrate, perivascular cuffing or sheets of large atypical lymphoid cells
Small round blue cell tumour centred on SKULL BONE or dura, invading the brain secondarily — not a parenchymal tumour
options.reason: A peripheral primitive neuroectodermal / Ewing sarcoma family tumour arising in bone belongs in ICCC-3 Group VIII (malignant bone tumours), subgroup VIIIc1, not in Group III. Code it from the Group VIII tree. Group III's 9473/3 is the CNS embryonal tumour code and applies only to a tumour arising in the brain itself.

options.descriptor: Small round blue cell tumour centred on EXTRADURAL SOFT TISSUE or scalp, invading the skull and brain secondarily
options.reason: A peripheral primitive neuroectodermal / Ewing sarcoma family tumour arising in soft tissue belongs in ICCC-3 Group IX (soft tissue sarcomas), subgroup IXd1, not in Group III. Code it from the Group IX tree.

options.descriptor: Clearly non-neuroepithelial — gland-forming or keratinising carcinoma, melanoma, or another morphology foreign to the CNS
options.reason: This is a metastasis, not a primary intracranial neoplasm. Go back to Stage 1 and code the PRIMARY tumour in the group that owns it. Only where no primary is ever established does the case sit outside Group III as 8000/3 at C80.9. Never emit 8000/6 or 8000/9 — both fall outside this group's 0-1,3 behaviour declaration.

options.descriptor: The file records an obsolete or superseded diagnosis and no material remains — code it as documented
On review this is not a neoplasm — abscess, tuberculoma, demyelination or cortical dysplasia

options.label: Mesenchymal / sarcomatoid - spindle, pleomorphic or rhabdoid cells with no glial or neuronal differentiation; GFAP and OLIG2 negative where stained
options.coding_note: Added 2026-09-15. Routes to the shared node st_dicer1_sarcoma. Primary intracranial sarcoma, DICER1-mutant is 92% supratentorial with a median age of 6 years, so every compartment that can carry it reaches the node; g3_midline deliberately does not.

options.descriptor: A malignant tumour is present but no morphological family can be assigned — the tissue is too scanty, too crushed or too necrotic to type, though malignancy is not in doubt

diagnosis_rendering.comment: Malignancy is established on tissue but no morphological family is. This is ICCC-3 IIIf, the subgroup a resource-limited registry reaches most often; it is a real answer, not a failure, and it must be recorded with its evidence tier so it is not compared across site profiles.

provisional_pending.reason: No morphological family was established. Review of the block, deeper levels, or a basic lineage panel (GFAP, synaptophysin, EMA, Olig2) would place the case in a family.

options.descriptor: A neoplasm is present but neither its family nor its behaviour can be assigned

diagnosis_rendering.comment: Tissue establishes a neoplasm and nothing more. Behaviour is not asserted: this registry registers non-malignant CNS neoplasms, so 8000/1 records the case honestly rather than forcing a malignant code onto an unestablished behaviour.

provisional_pending.reason: Neither family nor behaviour is established. A basic lineage panel would place the case in a family; where it does not, the case stays at 8000/1.

nodes.question: The infiltrate is lymphoid. What does the lineage panel show?
nodes.hint: A primary CNS lymphoma is a real cancer, but it is not a Group III tumour. EBV-associated CNS lymphoma is common where HIV prevalence is high, so a dense perivascular lymphoid infiltrate in this setting is lymphoma until proved otherwise — not a glioma with reactive lymphocytes.
nodes.coding_note: Master file dual-group rules: primary CNS lymphoma is ICCC-3 Group II. Group III must emit no code for it.

marker_groups.group_label: Glial and neuronal — read to exclude a glioma with a reactive lymphoid component

resolution_logic.reason: CD20-positive, CD3-negative — a primary CNS B-cell lymphoma. This belongs in ICCC-3 Group II (lymphomas and reticuloendothelial neoplasms), not Group III. Code it from the Group II tree, where primary diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of the CNS and the immunodeficiency-associated CNS lymphomas are carried. Where HIV prevalence is high this is a common supratentorial mass and EBER should be recorded with it.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Do not emit a Group III code here. Record the EBER result in the Group II tree, where it is entity-defining.

resolution_logic.reason: CD3-positive, CD20-negative — a primary CNS T-cell lymphoma. This belongs in ICCC-3 Group II, not Group III. Code it from the Group II tree.

resolution_logic.coding_note: A glial tumour with a reactive lymphoid component, not a lymphoma. Return to the family gate and take the glial branch.

diagnosis_rendering.comment: A lymphoid-appearing malignant infiltrate on which the lineage panel did not resolve. The case is recorded at IIIf rather than assigned to either a glial or a lymphoid code on morphology alone.

provisional_pending.reason: Lineage is unresolved. A repeat panel on a fresh block (CD45, CD20, CD3, GFAP) would separate a primary CNS lymphoma, which leaves Group III for Group II, from a glial tumour, which stays here.

nos_fallback.name: Neoplasm, uncertain whether benign or malignant
nos_fallback.reason: The lineage panel did not resolve and neither a lymphoid nor a glial assignment is defensible. 8000/3 records the malignancy without asserting a lineage; a Group III glial code here would file a lymphoma in the wrong group.

nodes.step_label: Histologic grade of the diffuse glioma
nodes.question: On the H&E alone, is this diffuse glioma low grade or high grade?
nodes.hint: Grade first, type second. In a child the molecular shortcuts that define an adult glioblastoma do NOT apply: cIMPACT-NOW update 11 says a TERT promoter mutation is not a solitary defining feature in a histologically low-grade tumour at any age, and EGFR amplification and +7/-10 are not solitary defining features below 40 years. Below 18, none of the three stands alone. Grade this on the slide.
nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 §4.3. The Santosh rule allowing glioblastoma IDH-wildtype to be assigned at RL III on histology alone is scoped to 55 years and over and NEVER applies in this registry — no such branch exists in this tree (Revision 2 §1.7).

options.descriptor: LOW grade — no or isolated mitoses, no microvascular proliferation, no necrosis
HIGH grade — brisk mitoses, microvascular proliferation, or necrosis
The grade cannot be assessed — the biopsy is too small, crushed or cauterised to grade, though a diffuse glial tumour is established

diagnosis_rendering.comment: A diffuse glial tumour is established on tissue but the material will not carry a grade. No grade is asserted rather than one guessed. At C71.x, 9380/3 is ICCC-3 IIId2.

provisional_pending.reason: The grade is unestablished, and with it the whole paediatric-type differential: a low-grade and a high-grade tumour take different branches from here. Deeper levels or a repeat biopsy would resolve it.

nodes.question: What does the panel show on this low-grade diffuse glioma?
nodes.hint: CNS5 split the diffuse gliomas into adult-type and paediatric-type. In a child the paediatric-type families come first: PLNTY, angiocentric glioma, diffuse astrocytoma MYB- or MYBL1-altered, and diffuse low-grade glioma MAPK pathway-altered. None of the four has an ICD-O-3.2 code — each is recorded as an entity annotation against a code chosen by grade.
nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 §4.3. Resource level for the paediatric-type diffuse gliomas is assigned BY ANALOGY: ADAPTR's Santosh paper covers adult-type diffuse gliomas and states only that its recommendations 'can also be applied to adolescents and children likely to have ADGs'. Every node in this family therefore carries rl_assignment by_analogy.

marker_groups.group_label: H&E pattern — tick what the report actually describes
markers: Cortical or temporal location in drug-resistant epilepsy

marker_groups.group_label: Surrogate molecular IHC (RL III) — CD34 is scored as STRONG only when staining is strong AND diffuse in tumour cells; ATRX is ticked when nuclear expression is LOST

resolution_logic.coding_note: The PLNTY constellation: infiltrative oligodendroglioma-like H&E with strong diffuse CD34 and a negative IDH1 R132H. 1p/19q is the last member of the minimum test set and is asked next.
Angiocentric glioma: perivascular bipolar pseudorosettes with GFAP positivity and dot-like EMA are the essential criteria. MYB::QKI (12 of 14 cases) is confirmatory, not required.
The DGONC constellation. DGONC is a PROVISIONAL CNS5 type with no ICD-O-3.2 code; monosomy 14 or a methylation class is what names it.
The DLGNT constellation. 1p deletion plus a MAPK alteration is what names it; it has no ICD-O-3.2 code.

Oligodendroglioma-like cytology without strong diffuse CD34. In a child this is more likely PLNTY, DLGNT, DGONC, clear cell ependymoma or extraventricular neurocytoma than a true oligodendroglioma — the oligodendroglial node routes that differential before it reaches 9450.

An IDH1 R132H-positive low-grade diffuse glioma is an ADULT-TYPE diffuse glioma and is rare below 18. 1p/19q separates astrocytoma, IDH-mutant from oligodendroglioma, IDH-mutant, and 1p/19q-codeleted.
Nothing in the panel names a family. The molecular gate asks for MYB/MYBL1 and the MAPK pathway, which are what the two remaining paediatric-type low-grade entities turn on.

nos_fallback.name: Astrocytoma, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: A low-grade diffuse glioma with a panel that names no paediatric-type entity. 9400/3 is the grade-appropriate family NOS code; the entity is left unstated rather than guessed.

nodes.step_label: PLNTY — the last member of the minimum test set
nodes.question: Has 1p/19q codeletion been tested, and what did it show?
nodes.hint: PLNTY needs four things together: an infiltrative oligodendroglioma-like H&E, strong diffuse CD34, a negative IDH1 R132H, and the ABSENCE of 1p/19q codeletion. Three of the four are already in. Without the fourth the honest answer is a descriptive low-grade glial/glioneuronal diagnosis, not PLNTY.
nodes.coding_note: PLNTY has no ICD-O-3.2 code. CNS5 Table 3 grades it 1, so it resolves to 9400/3 with the entity carried as an annotation (Revision 2 §4.3, §1.2).

options.label: IDH1 R132H was PERFORMED and is negative, AND 1p/19q was tested and is NOT codeleted

diagnosis_rendering.who_diagnosis: Polymorphous low-grade neuroepithelial tumor of the young

entity_annotation.who_cns5_entity: Polymorphous low-grade neuroepithelial tumor of the young
entity_annotation.evidence: Infiltrative oligodendroglioma-like histology with strong diffuse CD34, IDH1 R132H negative, and 1p/19q codeletion excluded

options.label: 1p/19q tested — CODELETED
options.coding_note: A 1p/19q-codeleted tumour is not PLNTY. Route it through the oligodendroglial molecular gate, where IDH status decides between the codeleted CNS5 entity and a paediatric-type tumour.

options.label: IDH1 R132H was not performed, or its control failed — so it is neither positive nor negative

diagnosis_rendering.comment: Strong diffuse CD34 in an infiltrative oligodendroglioma-like tumour raises PLNTY, but a stain that was not performed is not a negative stain and IDH1 R132H is part of the minimum test set. The WHO CNS5 diagnosis is not made.

provisional_pending.reason: IDH1 R132H immunohistochemistry is an RL III test and is the cheapest outstanding member of the PLNTY minimum test set. 1p/19q codeletion must then also be excluded.
alternative_entities: Polymorphous low-grade neuroepithelial tumor of the young

options.label: IDH1 R132H is negative, but 1p/19q could not be tested — no FISH, no fresh tissue, or the assay failed

diagnosis_rendering.comment: Strong diffuse CD34 with a negative IDH1 R132H in an infiltrative oligodendroglioma-like tumour is highly suggestive of PLNTY, but 1p/19q codeletion has not been excluded and the WHO CNS5 diagnosis is therefore not made.

provisional_pending.reason: PLNTY requires 1p/19q codeletion to be excluded. Until it is, an oligodendroglioma and the other oligodendroglioma-like paediatric tumours stay open.

nos_fallback.name: Astrocytoma, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: The PLNTY minimum test set is incomplete and no other entity is named. 9400/3 is the grade-appropriate family NOS code.

nodes.question: Has a MYB::QKI fusion been sought, and what did the essential criteria show?
nodes.hint: The essential criteria for angiocentric glioma are morphological and are already met at RL II: perivascular bipolar pseudorosettes, GFAP positivity and dot-like EMA. MYB::QKI is confirmatory — it was present in 12 of 14 cases, so a negative result does not overturn the diagnosis.
nodes.coding_note: 9431/1 is a /1 code and is registrable under the 14-09-26 ruling. Angiocentric glioma is also a documented DIPG mimic with a median age of 5 years, which is why it is one of the diversion criteria on the imaging endpoint in the posterior fossa tree.

options.label: MYB::QKI fusion DETECTED
MYB::QKI tested — NOT detected, and the morphological criteria are all met
options.coding_note: MYB::QKI was present in 12 of 14 cases, so 2 of 14 angiocentric gliomas do not carry it. A negative fusion does not overturn a diagnosis whose essential criteria are morphological.

options.label: MYB::QKI not tested, but the morphological criteria are all met — pseudorosettes, GFAP and dot-like EMA

provisional_pending.reason: The diagnosis rests on morphology and basic IHC, which is the essential criterion set. MYB::QKI would confirm it and is the only test outstanding.

options.label: Dot-like EMA or GFAP is not documented — the angiocentric pattern is the only finding

diagnosis_rendering.comment: An angiocentric growth pattern is described but the essential criterion set is incomplete, so the WHO CNS5 diagnosis is not made. 9431/1 is the code the pattern belongs to.

provisional_pending.reason: GFAP and EMA complete the essential criteria and are both RL II tests; MYB::QKI would then confirm the entity.

nos_fallback.name: Angiocentric glioma
nos_fallback.reason: The angiocentric pattern is the established finding and 9431/1 is the code it belongs to, whether or not the fusion was sought.

nodes.question: What molecular testing was done on this low-grade diffuse glioma, and what did it show?
nodes.hint: Two paediatric-type entities are decided here. Diffuse astrocytoma, MYB- or MYBL1-altered needs a demonstrated MYB or MYBL1 alteration with IDH and H3 both wildtype. Diffuse low-grade glioma, MAPK pathway-altered needs a MAPK alteration AND the absence of IDH1/2, H3F3A and CDKN2A homozygous deletion. Neither has an ICD-O-3.2 code.
nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 §4.3 and §1.2. Both entities resolve to 9400/3 with the CNS5 entity carried as an annotation at code_status no_code.

options.label: MYB or MYBL1 alteration demonstrated, with IDH wildtype and H3 wildtype

entity_annotation.evidence: Demonstrated MYB or MYBL1 alteration with IDH-wildtype and H3-wildtype status

options.coding_note: CNS5 Table 3 grades this entity 1 — which is why the Arabic grade set must include 1. Behaves indolently; the tumour must not be escalated on the strength of its infiltrative appearance.

options.label: A MAPK-pathway alteration demonstrated (BRAF fusion, BRAF p.V600E, FGFR1 or NF1), with no IDH1/2 mutation, no H3F3A mutation and no CDKN2A homozygous deletion

entity_annotation.evidence: A MAPK-pathway alteration with IDH1/2, H3F3A and CDKN2A homozygous deletion all absent

options.coding_note: CNS5 assigns this type no definite grade, so none is emitted. The absence of CDKN2A homozygous deletion is part of the definition, not an afterthought.

options.label: An IDH1 or IDH2 mutation was demonstrated
options.coding_note: An IDH-mutant diffuse glioma is adult-type and rare below 18. 1p/19q decides between astrocytoma, IDH-mutant and oligodendroglioma, IDH-mutant, and 1p/19q-codeleted.

options.label: MYB/MYBL1 and a MAPK panel were both performed and both were negative, with IDH and H3 wildtype

diagnosis_rendering.comment: An adequate molecular result was obtained and it maps to no WHO CNS5 type. cIMPACT-NOW update 1 makes this NEC, not NOS: the testing was done and the tumour did not fit.

options.coding_note: NEC is earned here because the tests returned. A registry that could not run them may never emit NEC.

options.label: No molecular testing is available for this case

diagnosis_rendering.comment: A low-grade diffuse glioma in a child with no molecular testing. Do NOT escalate this tumour on its infiltrative appearance: the commonest paediatric-type low-grade entities behave indolently, and the diagnosis is NOS because the tests were unavailable, not because the tumour is aggressive.

provisional_pending.reason: MYB/MYBL1 and the MAPK pathway are both untested, so two paediatric-type CNS5 entities remain open. Both are reachable at RL IV.

nos_fallback.name: Astrocytoma, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: A low-grade diffuse glioma whose molecular gate did not resolve. 9400/3 is the grade-appropriate family NOS code.

nodes.question: The tumour has clear cells with perinuclear haloes. What else does the panel and the H&E show?
nodes.hint: True IDH-mutant, 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendroglioma is RARE in children. An oligodendroglioma-like paediatric tumour is more likely PLNTY, DLGNT, DGONC, clear cell ependymoma or extraventricular neurocytoma. Work that differential before reaching for 9450 — fried-egg cells are not a diagnosis.
nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 §4.8, the paediatric caveat the previous revision lacked. Clear cell ependymoma is a Related term of 9391/3, not a code of its own; extraventricular neurocytoma is a Related term of 9506/1.

marker_groups.group_label: H&E pattern — tick what the report describes
Surrogate molecular IHC (RL III) — CD34 is scored STRONG only when staining is strong AND diffuse; ATRX is ticked when nuclear expression is LOST

resolution_logic.coding_note: Strong diffuse CD34 in an infiltrative oligodendroglioma-like tumour is the PLNTY constellation, not an oligodendroglioma.
A uniform synaptophysin- and NeuN-positive intraventricular tumour with perinuclear haloes is a central neurocytoma, not an oligodendroglioma. 9506/1 is registrable under the 14-09-26 ruling.
Extraventricular neurocytoma is a Related term of 9506/1 and has no code of its own.

provisional_pending.reason: Synaptophysin and NeuN positivity in a clear-cell tumour supports a neurocytoma. Where Olig2 and GFAP were not run, a clear cell ependymoma and an oligodendroglioma-like paediatric tumour are not yet excluded — an unrun stain is not a negative stain.
alternative_entities: Polymorphous low-grade neuroepithelial tumor of the young

resolution_logic.coding_note: Clear cell ependymoma. CNS5 demoted clear cell, papillary and tanycytic ependymoma from subtypes to morphological patterns, and ICD-O-3.2 agrees — clear cell ependymoma is a Related term of 9391/3.
The DLGNT constellation.
The DGONC constellation. DGONC is a provisional CNS5 type.
Nothing in the panel names one of the oligodendroglioma-like paediatric entities. IDH and 1p/19q are what separate a true oligodendroglioma from a paediatric-type diffuse glioma.

nos_fallback.name: Oligodendroglioma, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: An oligodendroglioma-like tumour whose panel resolved nothing. 9450/3 records the morphology; the CNS5 entity is not asserted, because IDH and 1p/19q are what would establish it.

nodes.question: What did IDH and 1p/19q testing show?
nodes.hint: Where both are unavailable — which is the usual case — the honest output is 9450/3 with a named provisional and low confidence, not a molecular diagnosis. The RL III surrogate route (HIP1R, vimentin, H3 K27me3) approximates 1p/19q status; it does not establish it, and no branch here rests on it.
nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 §4.8. Note the two strings that differ by one comma and live in different fields: ICD-O-3.2's Related term of 9450/3 is 'Oligodendroglioma, IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted'; CNS5 Table 1 prints 'Oligodendroglioma, IDH-mutant, and 1p/19q-codeleted'. Never substitute one for the other.

options.label: IDH1/2 MUTANT and 1p/19q CODELETED — no brisk mitoses, no microvascular proliferation, no necrosis
options.coding_note: Rare below 18. 9450/3's ICD-O-3.2 Related term is 'Oligodendroglioma, IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted' — one comma fewer than the CNS5 Table 1 string used in the rendered diagnosis.

options.label: IDH1/2 MUTANT and 1p/19q CODELETED — with brisk mitoses, microvascular proliferation or necrosis
options.coding_note: CNS5 DELETED anaplastic oligodendroglioma as a type — grade is now expressed within the type, exactly as it deleted anaplastic astrocytoma and anaplastic ependymoma. The code 9451/3 still exists and is what carries a grade 3 oligodendroglioma; the diagnosis string 'anaplastic oligodendroglioma' does not.

options.label: IDH1/2 MUTANT, 1p/19q NOT codeleted

shared_with: Polymorphous low-grade neuroepithelial tumor of the young
entity_annotation.evidence: IDH1/2 mutation with 1p/19q codeletion excluded

options.coding_note: 9445/3 Glioblastoma, IDH-mutant names a type CNS5 ABOLISHED and must never be assigned prospectively, and never to a child. A grade 4 IDH-mutant astrocytoma is reached through the high-grade branch, which emits 9401/3 with the grade resolved separately.

options.label: IDH1/2 WILDTYPE
options.coding_note: An IDH-wildtype diffuse glioma in a child is a paediatric-type tumour. CNS5: 'In IDH-wildtype diffuse astrocytomas occurring in younger age groups, consideration should be given to the different types of diffuse pediatric-type gliomas.'

options.label: Neither IDH nor 1p/19q could be tested

diagnosis_rendering.comment: Oligodendroglial morphology with neither IDH nor 1p/19q established. The WHO CNS5 diagnosis requires both, and in a child the differential — PLNTY, DLGNT, DGONC, clear cell ependymoma, extraventricular neurocytoma — is wider than in an adult, so this is a morphological label and not a molecular one.

provisional_pending.reason: BOTH defining tests are outstanding: IDH1/2 sequencing (or IDH1 R132H immunohistochemistry as a first pass) and 1p/19q codeletion by FISH. Santosh's RL III surrogate panel approximates 1p/19q status but does not establish it, so it cannot close this provisional.
alternative_entities: Polymorphous low-grade neuroepithelial tumor of the young
Diffuse glioneuronal tumor with oligodendroglioma-like features and nuclear clusters

nos_fallback.name: Oligodendroglioma, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Oligodendroglial morphology with the molecular gate unresolved. 9450/3 records the morphology and asserts no molecular type.

nodes.question: What does the surrogate molecular panel show on this high-grade diffuse glioma?
nodes.hint: Two stains decide most of this node and both are RL III. H3 K27M names a diffuse midline glioma outright; H3 G34R/V names a diffuse hemispheric glioma. Neither TERT, nor EGFR amplification, nor +7/-10 defines a glioblastoma on its own in a child, so no branch here rests on one of them.
nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 §4.3. C71.0 carries thalamus and basal ganglia, so a thalamic H3 K27-altered tumour reaches this node and must be coded 9385/3, which moves it from ICCC-3 IIIb to IIId2 — a test-availability artefact (§1.5) that must not be read epidemiologically. An H3 K27M-positive tumour with EPENDYMAL morphology and dot-like EMA is a PFA ependymoma, not a diffuse midline glioma; that tumour belongs in the posterior fossa tree.

marker_groups.group_label: H&E pattern — tick what the report describes
markers: Thalamic, basal ganglia or other midline location
Desmoplastic, superficial, with a large cystic component

marker_groups.group_label: Surrogate molecular IHC (RL III) — ATRX is ticked when nuclear expression is LOST

entity_annotation.evidence: H3 G34R/V immunohistochemistry positive

resolution_logic.coding_note: No ICD-O-3.2 code exists for this entity; it resolves to 9440/3 by grade with the entity carried as an annotation. The code 9440/3 is correct; the diagnosis string 'glioblastoma' is not — CNS5 states that the term is no longer used in the setting of a paediatric-type neoplasm, and the rendered diagnosis above says so.

ICD-O-3.2's preferred term for 9385/3 is still 'Diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27M-mutant'; CNS5 renamed the entity H3 K27-altered. The code is right and the rendered diagnosis uses the CNS5 name. This moves the case from ICCC-3 IIIb to IIId2 — the same tumour without the stain would have been 9440/3 in IIIb.

grade_resolution.criterion: CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion in an IDH-mutant astrocytoma raises the grade to CNS WHO grade 4 with no histological change

hemizygous_or_absent.reason: Hemizygous deletion is explicitly excluded by cIMPACT-NOW update 12; it does not raise the grade, and the histological grade stands.

resolution_logic.coding_note: 9445/3 Glioblastoma, IDH-mutant names an entity CNS5 ABOLISHED — such tumours are Astrocytoma, IDH-mutant, CNS WHO grade 4. It must never be assigned prospectively and never to a child, so a grade 4 IDH-mutant astrocytoma is coded 9401/3 with the grade carried in grade_resolution. Historical 9445 entries at paediatric ages are flagged for review, not migrated: under the superseded revision's instruction they may be mis-entered pleomorphic xanthoastrocytomas.

Under 3 with a hemispheric high-grade glioma: infant-type hemispheric glioma and DIG/DIA are the differential, and histology alone cannot separate them — 2 of 5 histological DIG/DIA in Gilani 2023 were IHG. 'Congenital glioblastoma' is abolished and must not be used.
H3-wildtype and IDH-wildtype so far. cIMPACT-NOW update 11 asks that mismatch-repair immunohistochemistry be CONSIDERED at this point in a patient under 18 — it is asked next, and it may be declined.

nos_fallback.name: Glioblastoma, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: A high-grade diffuse glioma on which the surrogate panel named no entity. 9440/3 is the grade-appropriate family NOS code — the code is permissible; the diagnosis string 'glioblastoma' is not used for a paediatric-type neoplasm.

nodes.step_label: Mismatch-repair IHC — a consideration, not a requirement
nodes.question: cIMPACT-NOW update 11 says mismatch-repair immunohistochemistry SHOULD BE CONSIDERED in a patient under 18 with an H3-wildtype high-grade glioma. Was it done, and what did it show?
nodes.hint: 'Should be considered' is the WEAKEST of the three recommendation tiers — this is not an obligation and the case proceeds either way. Tick a protein only where nuclear expression is LOST in tumour cells with a retained internal control. The result changes no code; it is recorded because it carries a germline implication.
nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 §1.7: this is the ONE sub-18 rule in the whole cIMPACT-NOW series, and because it is IHC-only it is reachable at RL II and above — one of the few universal recommendations this registry can actually act on. It applies to IDH-mutant astrocytomas as well as to H3-wildtype high-grade gliomas.

marker_groups.group_label: Mismatch-repair proteins — tick where nuclear expression is LOST in tumour cells and retained in the internal control

resolution_logic.coding_note: MSH2 loss. Record the germline referral flag; the code is unchanged.
MSH6 loss. Record the germline referral flag; the code is unchanged.
MLH1 loss. Record the germline referral flag; the code is unchanged.
PMS2 loss. Record the germline referral flag; the code is unchanged.
All four retained, or the panel was not performed. Either way the case proceeds: the recommendation tier is 'can be considered' and the result changes no code.

nos_fallback.name: Glioblastoma, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Mismatch-repair status changes no code. 9440/3 remains the grade-appropriate family NOS code for a high-grade diffuse glioma while the type is resolved.

nodes.question: Is DNA methylation profiling available for this case, and what did it return?
nodes.hint: Two CNS5 entities are reachable ONLY here and only at RL V: diffuse paediatric-type high-grade glioma, H3-wildtype and IDH-wildtype, and high-grade astrocytoma with piloid features. Where methylation profiling is not available, say so — the test is unavailable, not pending.
nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 §4.0 and §4.3. cIMPACT-NOW update 11 makes methylation essential for the paediatric-type high-grade glioma entity. Neither entity has an ICD-O-3.2 code; both resolve to 9440/3 by grade.

options.label: Methylation profiling performed — the class is diffuse paediatric-type high-grade glioma, H3-wildtype and IDH-wildtype

diagnosis_rendering.who_diagnosis: Diffuse pediatric-type high-grade glioma, H3-wildtype and IDH-wildtype

entity_annotation.who_cns5_entity: Diffuse pediatric-type high-grade glioma, H3-wildtype and IDH-wildtype
entity_annotation.evidence: DNA methylation class assignment with H3 and IDH both wildtype

options.coding_note: CNS5 Table 1's spelling has NO comma before 'and'; Table 2 prints the same entity with one. Table 1 wins.

options.label: Methylation profiling performed — the class is high-grade astrocytoma with piloid features

entity_annotation.evidence: DNA methylation class assignment

options.coding_note: CNS5 assigns this methylome-defined type no definite grade, so none is emitted.

nodes.question: What does the ependymal panel show?
nodes.hint: In this compartment the surrogate markers yield NEGATIVE conclusions only. L1CAM and p65/RelA both negative EXCLUDES a ZFTA fusion (negative predictive value 100%, n = 42). They cannot assert one: single-marker positive predictive value is 73-91.7% and the combination 86.2-92.5%, and all three primary papers demand molecular confirmation. YAP1 fusion has no positive immunohistochemical surrogate with any performance data at all.
nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 §4.1. Lim 2022's rule that all L1CAM-positive cases are ZFTA-positive is REJECTED and no branch implements it. Chinnam's two-of-three rule (any two of L1CAM, p65/RelA, cyclin D1) lifts sensitivity from 92.3% to 96.2% and the negative predictive value to 96.6% — it strengthens the suspicion, it does not establish the fusion. Note also that YAP1 here is the supratentorial ependymoma FUSION PARTNER, a different thing entirely from the YAP1 immunostain used as a medulloblastoma molecular-group surrogate in the posterior fossa tree.

nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 4.11, Sood 2024 and Korbonits 2024. Lineage assignment is reachable at RL III. options.coding_note: TOPOGRAPHY SPLIT. 9380/3 is IIIb at C72.3 and IIId2 at every other CNS site. This node is reachable only from C72.3, so the case is IIIb.

options.descriptor: The specimen shows optic nerve tissue with no tumour

nodes.question: Olfactory, acoustic or other cranial nerve lesion (C72.2, C72.4, C72.5). What does the file establish?
nodes.hint: Most lesions at these three topographies leave Group III. Inside the group they are reachable only through IIId2 - the mixed and unspecified gliomas - and IIIf. The two that will actually arrive are olfactory neuroblastoma and vestibular schwannoma, and neither is a Group III tumour.
nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 3.1. Every referral carries its explanation in reason, which the engine renders; coding_note is author-facing and is not displayed, so a referral written there would arrive with no explanation of where to send the case.

options.descriptor: Olfactory neuroblastoma / esthesioneuroblastoma of the olfactory nerve or cribriform plate
options.reason: Olfactory neuroblastoma is ICCC-3 group IVb, other peripheral nervous cell tumours, not Group III. No Group III code is emitted and the case is coded in Group IV. The topography stays C72.2 where the tumour arises from the olfactory nerve.

options.descriptor: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumour of a cranial nerve
options.reason: A malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumour is ICCC-3 group IXb2, nerve sheath tumours, not Group III. No Group III code is emitted and the case is coded in Group IX.

options.descriptor: Vestibular schwannoma / acoustic neuroma - benign
options.reason: A benign schwannoma is a real neoplasm but it is outside this classification in both directions: 9560 is not in any ICCC-3 Group III code range, and ICCC-3 group IXb2 declares behaviour 3 only, so a /0 schwannoma is not in Group IX either. No Group III code is emitted and the case does not enter the malignant registry. This is NOT a finding that the lesion is non-neoplastic - if the registry keeps a separate non-malignant CNS register, the case belongs on it. Raised for the registrar: this tree has no terminal that says 'a neoplasm, outside this classification' as distinct from 'not a neoplasm'.

options.descriptor: Malignant glioma of a cranial nerve, type not stated

diagnosis_rendering.comment: A malignant glioma at a cranial nerve topography other than the optic nerve. The report states neither type nor grade, so neither is rendered.

options.upgrade_path: GFAP, OLIG2 and Ki-67 at RL II would place the tumour in a family.
options.coding_note: TOPOGRAPHY SPLIT. 9380/3 is IIId2 at C72.2, C72.4 and C72.5 - IIIb is reserved for C72.3, which this node never sees. This is one of the two routes by which a cranial nerve lesion stays inside Group III.

options.descriptor: Astrocytoma of a cranial nerve

diagnosis_rendering.comment: Astrocytic morphology at a cranial nerve topography. No molecular testing has been performed, so no WHO CNS5 type is rendered and the grade is the ADAPTR histologic grade.

options.upgrade_path: A paediatric-type diffuse glioma panel would be the next step.

options.descriptor: Pilocytic astrocytoma of a cranial nerve
options.upgrade_path: None outstanding for the code.
options.coding_note: 9421/1 - IIIb, registrable under the 14-09-26 ruling.

options.descriptor: A malignant neoplasm is established at this cranial nerve but the type is not

diagnosis_rendering.comment: Malignancy is established and the type is not. 8000/3 is the IIIf code at this topography and carries the group's unspecified-neoplasm flag.

provisional_pending.reason: The tumour type is not established. Record whether surgery was performed, whether tissue reached pathology, whether immunohistochemistry was requested, and whether the result was unavailable or not requested.

options.upgrade_path: A basic lineage panel at RL II - GFAP, S100, synaptophysin, EMA - would place the tumour.
options.coding_note: IIIf. 8000 is authored at /0, /1 and /3 only; /6 and /9 fall outside the group's 0-1,3 declaration.

options.descriptor: A neoplasm is established at this cranial nerve but neither the type nor the behaviour is

diagnosis_rendering.comment: Neither type nor behaviour is established. 8000/1 is inside the group - ICCC-3 declares Group III behaviours 0-1,3 - so nothing is lost by recording the uncertainty rather than resolving it.

options.upgrade_path: A basic lineage panel at RL II would place the tumour.
options.coding_note: IIIf.

options.descriptor: The lesion is a metastasis from a known primary elsewhere
options.reason: Code the primary, not the biopsy site. No Group III code is emitted: 8000/6 and 8000/9 fall outside this group's 0-1,3 behaviour declaration, so a case carrying them would leave Group III silently. Re-enter the tool at the primary site.

options.descriptor: The file establishes a non-neoplastic cranial nerve lesion

nodes.question: What exactly does the referral or clinic letter say?
nodes.hint: A referral naming an entity is not the same as a report establishing it, and in this compartment that gap is wide: 22.6% of institutional pineoblastoma diagnoses were other entities. The wording chooses which gate runs next; it does not choose a code.
nodes.coding_note: No code is emitted from the wording for any entity in this compartment. The germ cell marker gate runs first in every case, because a referral saying 'pineal tumour' is exactly the case Revision 2 3.2 exists for.

options.label: 'Pineal tumour', 'pineoblastoma', 'pineocytoma' or 'pineal region mass'
'Craniopharyngioma' or 'suprasellar cystic mass'
'Pituitary adenoma', 'prolactinoma', 'Cushing disease' or 'sellar mass'
options.coding_note: 'Prolactinoma' is a clinical synonym; 8271/0's ICD-O-3.2 preferred term is Lactotroph adenoma and that is what the tool emits.

options.label: 'Optic pathway glioma', 'optic nerve glioma' or 'chiasmatic glioma'
'Acoustic neuroma', 'vestibular schwannoma' or 'olfactory neuroblastoma'
The letter names no entity - 'midline mass for investigation', 'awaiting biopsy'

diagnosis_rendering.comment: A referral letter naming no entity and no investigation. Nothing is established beyond a mass at a Group III topography, and the basis of diagnosis is recorded as unknown rather than as a clinical examination - no Group III terminal may emit basis 1.

provisional_pending.reason: Nothing is established. No imaging report, no markers and no tissue are in the file.

options.upgrade_path: Serum and CSF αFP and β-hCG first, then the MRI report. Those two answer the Group X question and fix the compartment, which is everything this tree needs to start.

nodes.question: What did the frozen section or squash cytology report, and did a definitive paraffin report follow?
nodes.hint: An intraoperative diagnosis is never the coded diagnosis where a definitive report exists. Where none ever follows it stands as cytology at basis of diagnosis 5, with the code capped at NOS level, and it must not be promoted to basis 7. Jain 2022 measured frozen section sensitivity at 91.43% and squash cytology at 88.57% in paediatric CNS tumours - craniopharyngioma was 6 of 6 correct by both, and a yolk sac tumour was 0 of 1 by both.
nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 3.4. ADAPTR places squash, smear and frozen section at RL I, alongside H&E, so a site with no immunohistochemistry still has an intraoperative capability and the tool should use it.

options.label: A definitive paraffin histology report also exists
options.coding_note: The intraoperative diagnosis is recorded as a separate field and the definitive report carries the code.

options.label: Squash or frozen reported a craniopharyngioma, and no definitive report ever followed

diagnosis_rendering.comment: Recorded on the intraoperative preparation alone at basis of diagnosis 5 (cytology). Craniopharyngioma was the best-performing entity in Jain's series - 6 of 6 correct by both frozen section and squash - but the type is not called on a smear, so the code is capped at 9350.

provisional_pending.reason: No definitive paraffin report exists. The diagnosis rests on the intraoperative preparation.

options.upgrade_path: Retrieve or process the paraffin block. That alone moves the basis of diagnosis from 5 to 7.

options.label: Squash or frozen reported a pituitary adenoma, and no definitive report ever followed

diagnosis_rendering.comment: Recorded on the intraoperative preparation alone at basis of diagnosis 5 (cytology). Neither tinctorial subtype nor transcription-factor lineage is callable on a smear, and no metastasis is documented, so the code is 8272/0.

provisional_pending.reason: No definitive paraffin report exists, and behaviour rests on the absence of a demonstrated metastasis rather than on its exclusion.

options.upgrade_path: Retrieve or process the paraffin block, then PIT1, TPIT and SF-1.

options.label: Squash or frozen reported a malignant tumour with the type not stated, and no definitive report ever followed

diagnosis_rendering.comment: Recorded on the intraoperative preparation alone at basis of diagnosis 5 (cytology), with the code capped at NOS level. A germ cell tumour is not excluded - Jain's single yolk sac tumour was called correctly by neither preparation.

provisional_pending.reason: No definitive paraffin report exists and no entity is established.

options.upgrade_path: Retrieve or process the paraffin block, and record the germ cell markers if they were taken.

options.label: The intraoperative preparation was non-diagnostic
options.coding_note: CROSS-TREE to g3_unspecified.

nodes.question: The imaging route does not carry this case. Is tissue available, or will none be obtained?
nodes.hint: Either a feature was ticked that requires tissue whatever the imaging shows, or the constellation was incomplete. Both mean the same thing here: the imaging alone is not enough for this case.
nodes.coding_note: Shared diversion and insufficiency target for every imaging_pathway node in this tree - md_pituitary_prolactin_route, md_pituitary_functioning_route, md_cranio_imaging, md_pineal_imaging_only and md_optic_nf1_imaging. One node rather than five keeps the no-tissue terminal in a single place.

options.label: A pituitary specimen is available or can be retrieved
A sellar or suprasellar specimen is available or can be retrieved
A pineal specimen is available or can be retrieved
An optic pathway specimen is available or can be retrieved
No tissue has been obtained and none will be

diagnosis_rendering.comment: Registered on imaging with no tissue examined and no imaging endpoint met. 8000/1 records a neoplasm of uncertain behaviour at a Group III topography; ENCR permits 8000/0 and 8000/1 as CNS defaults, and Group III's behaviour declaration of 0-1,3 keeps the case inside the group.

provisional_pending.reason: No tissue has been examined and no imaging endpoint is met. No entity is established.

options.upgrade_path: A biopsy is the only route from here. Record the germ cell markers alongside it.
options.coding_note: No-tissue terminal. Carries no_tissue, endpoint_verification and basis 2 exactly as the imaging_pathway terminals upstream do, because it is reached from them and rests on the same evidence.

options.label: On review the compartment is not established
options.coding_note: CROSS-TREE to g3_unspecified.

nodes.question: Which non-neoplastic lesion does the file establish?
nodes.hint: This exit is for lesions that are not neoplasms. It is NOT the exit for a benign tumour: craniopharyngioma, pituicytoma, granular cell tumour of the sellar region, pinealoma, pineocytoma, pilocytic astrocytoma and every /0 pituitary adenoma are registrable destinations in this tree, and sending one here would delete a real case from the registry.
nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 1.7. The non-reportable exit stopped being the destination for benign behaviour when register_nonmalignant_cns was set true on 14-09-26. It remains available for the genuinely non-neoplastic, which in a high-TB, high-HIV setting is not rare. Every option emits no code.

options.descriptor: Rathke cleft cyst - cyst lined by ciliated cuboidal or columnar epithelium with goblet cells, no squamous whorls and no wet keratin
options.reason: A Rathke cleft cyst is a developmental cyst, not a neoplasm. No morphology code is emitted and the case does not enter the registry. Where the wall shows squamous metaplasia with wet keratin the lesion is an adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma instead - re-read the section before accepting this exit.

options.descriptor: Arachnoid cyst
options.reason: An arachnoid cyst is a developmental cyst, not a neoplasm. No morphology code is emitted.

options.descriptor: Simple pineal cyst - a gliotic wall with no tumour
options.reason: A simple pineal cyst is not a neoplasm. No morphology code is emitted. Where the wall contains pineal parenchymal tumour cells the case is a pineal parenchymal tumour and belongs on the pineal branch.

options.descriptor: Hypophysitis - lymphocytic, granulomatous or IgG4-related inflammation of the pituitary
options.reason: Hypophysitis is inflammation, not a neoplasm. No morphology code is emitted. It is a recognised imaging mimic of a pituitary adenoma and of germinoma, so record it under its own name rather than as a negative result.

options.descriptor: Sellar or suprasellar tuberculoma, abscess or other granulomatous infection
options.reason: An infective mass is not a neoplasm. No morphology code is emitted. In a high-TB setting this is a real and recurring entry on the differential of a suprasellar mass, not a rarity.

options.descriptor: Optic neuritis or a demyelinating lesion of the optic nerve
options.reason: Demyelination is not a neoplasm. No morphology code is emitted.

options.descriptor: A non-neoplastic lesion that is not on this list
options.reason: The abstractor records that the file establishes a non-neoplastic lesion. No morphology code is emitted and the case does not enter the registry. Record the lesion under its own name. If the lesion is a benign NEOPLASM rather than a non-neoplastic one, go back: this exit is the wrong destination and would delete a registrable case.

options.descriptor: On review this is a neoplasm after all
options.coding_note: Returns to the compartment router rather than forcing a code from this node.

decision_trees.tree_label: Spinal cord and cauda equina — ependymal, piloid and diffuse glial tumours (C72.0, C72.1)

nodes.question: Spinal cord or cauda equina tumour. What reports are in this patient's file, and was the specimen adequate for diagnosis?
nodes.hint: Intraspinal biopsy carries real morbidity, so an inadequate or absent specimen is common here and it changes the code. Inadequate is not a negative result, and an uninterpretable section is not an inadequate one — pick the line that says what actually happened. A tumour that turns out to arise from a nerve root, a vertebra or a paraspinal mass is not a Group III primary; there is a line for that too.
nodes.coding_note: Entry node for tree g3_spinal, handed off by the router on C72.0 (spinal cord) or C72.1 (cauda equina). No extra topography question is asked of the clerk (contract §3). Basis-of-diagnosis declarations for the two ENCR gaps are carried here because basis is computed from this gate: IHC counts as 7, methylation profiling counts as 8 (Revision 2 §2.6).

options.label: Referral letter or clinical note only — no imaging report, no cytology and no histology
options.coding_note: Tier 1. Nothing above the family level is reachable from a referral, and a named entity in a referral is not a diagnosis.

options.label: MRI report only — no tissue was taken, and none is planned or available
options.coding_note: There is no imaging-only diagnostic endpoint in the spinal compartment. Revision 2 §3.5 grants exactly two, DIPG (pons) and NF1 optic pathway glioma (C72.3); neither is reachable from C72.0 or C72.1.

options.label: Intraoperative frozen section or squash cytology only — with or without a definitive paraffin report to follow
options.coding_note: Revision 2 §3.4: an intraoperative diagnosis is never the coded diagnosis. Frozen section sensitivity 91.43%, squash cytology 88.57%, kappa 0.729 (Jain 2022, paediatric CNS).

options.label: Definitive histology report — ADEQUATE specimen, H&E only, no immunohistochemistry available
options.coding_note: Resource level I for every family. Myxopapillary ependymoma and subependymoma are the two spinal types still reachable from morphology at this level (Revision 2 §4.0, §4.1).

options.label: Definitive histology report — ADEQUATE specimen, with immunohistochemistry (GFAP, EMA, Olig2, S100, synaptophysin and similar)
options.coding_note: Resource level II to III. Sufficient for myxopapillary ependymoma, subependymoma and spinal ependymoma; not sufficient for MYCN amplification or for 1p deletion.

options.label: Definitive histology report — ADEQUATE specimen, with immunohistochemistry AND FISH, RT-PCR or sequencing on fresh tissue
options.coding_note: Resource level IV or above. RL IV requires fresh tissue, not merely an assay contract (Revision 2 §2.2 rule 2) — a formalin-only pathway is not RL IV for MYCN or 1p FISH.

options.label: Biopsy taken but INADEQUATE — too little tissue, crush artefact, or the report says non-diagnostic
options.coding_note: Revision 2 §3.3. Resolves in the g3_unspecified tree to the group NOS code with a provisional_pending naming re-biopsy, and to basis of diagnosis 2, not 7 — the tissue did not yield a diagnosis. A crush-artefact biopsy is not a negative biopsy.

options.label: Biopsy taken but NOT ASSESSABLE — the section or the stains could not be read at all (processing failure, tissue exhausted, block lost)
options.coding_note: Distinct from inadequate: enough tissue may have been taken but no opinion could be given. Both owe a repeat; neither may close to a malignant NOS code from this node, and neither may be treated as a negative result.

options.label: The lesion is a deposit, a metastasis, a nerve sheath tumour, or a paraspinal or vertebral mass invading the canal
options.coding_note: These are not intraspinal CNS primaries and must not take a Group III code.

options.label: It cannot be established from the file that this is a spinal cord or cauda equina primary
options.coding_note: Compartment is a classification axis in this group (Revision 2 §3.1), so an unestablished site cannot be coded from a compartment tree.

nodes.question: What exactly does the referral or clinical note say?
nodes.hint: Code one level above whatever entity the note names. A referral that says myxopapillary ependymoma is a claim by someone who did not see the section; the honest ceiling is the family.
nodes.coding_note: Basis of diagnosis 2 throughout — clinical investigation without a tissue diagnosis. No Group III terminal may emit basis 1 (Revision 2 §2.6; ENCR Table 3 makes every CNS row basis 2). Confidence is low on every branch and every downstream test is an upgrade.

options.label: The note names an ependymoma of any kind — 'myxopapillary ependymoma', 'ependymoma', 'anaplastic ependymoma' — with no pathology report in the file

diagnosis_rendering.comment: Referral wording only. Ependymal lineage is asserted by the referrer and not confirmed on a section in this file. No grade is assigned because none was established.

options.upgrade_path: Histology with GFAP and EMA would confirm the ependymal type and give the CNS WHO grade; at the filum or conus it would separate myxopapillary ependymoma (9394/1) from spinal ependymoma.
options.coding_note: 9391/3 is the ependymal family root. Do not code the named subtype from a referral — myxopapillary ependymoma is 9394/1, a different behaviour as well as a different code, and reading it out of a letter changes the registry's malignant-only count.

options.label: The note names an astrocytoma, a glioma or a 'glial tumour' of the cord, with no pathology report

diagnosis_rendering.comment: Referral wording only. Glial lineage is asserted by the referrer; astrocytic lineage, grade and H3 K27M status are all unestablished.

options.upgrade_path: Histology with GFAP, Olig2 and H3 K27M would separate a diffuse midline glioma (9385/3) from a piloid tumour, and 1p FISH would separate a spinal piloid tumour from DLGNT.
options.coding_note: 9380/3 Glioma, malignant sits in IIId2 at C72.0 and C72.1 (it is IIIb only at C72.3). It is the honest ceiling from a referral — 9400/3 Astrocytoma, NOS asserts an astrocytic lineage nobody has demonstrated.

options.label: The note reads 'spinal cord tumour' or 'intramedullary tumour' — nothing about the type, and nothing about behaviour

diagnosis_rendering.comment: A tumour is asserted; neither its lineage nor its behaviour is established. Registrar ruling of 14 September 2026 registers non-malignant CNS neoplasms, so /1 keeps the case inside Group III rather than dropping it.

options.upgrade_path: Any tissue diagnosis replaces this. Imaging alone would at least fix the compartment and the sublocation.
options.coding_note: 8000/1 is IIIf. Report malignant-only and all-behaviour counts separately — Revision 2 §1.7.

options.label: The note reads 'malignant spinal cord tumour', 'spinal cancer' or similar — malignancy asserted, type not stated

diagnosis_rendering.comment: Malignancy is asserted clinically and no lineage is established. Behaviour /3 follows the referral's own claim.

options.upgrade_path: Histology would establish the lineage and, with IHC, the type.
options.coding_note: 8000/3 is IIIf. Metastatic disease is coded to the primary at Stage 1 — 8000/6 and 8000/9 fall outside this group's 0-1,3 behaviour declaration and must never be emitted here.

options.label: The note reads only 'back pain', 'paraparesis for investigation', 'cord compression' or similar — no diagnosis is asserted
options.coding_note: Not a tumour referral. It must pass the non-neoplastic gate before any code is considered — spinal abscess, tuberculoma and demyelination all present this way.

nodes.question: MRI only, no tissue. Confirm what the scan actually shows, and check the diversion list below before accepting any of these lines.
nodes.hint: MRI does not diagnose a spinal tumour type. The two imaging-only endpoints this group allows are DIPG in the pons and NF1 optic pathway glioma at C72.3, and neither is a spinal cord or cauda equina lesion. Anything on the diversion list sends the case to tissue whatever the scan looks like.
nodes.coding_note: Validation rule 11: every terminal reached here carries no_tissue true, endpoint_verification not_verified, basis_of_diagnosis 2 and a non-empty diversion_criteria list. ENCR Table 3 does permit 9391/3, 9392/3, 9394/1 and 9383/1 to be REGISTERED on imaging at basis 2; that is a registration permission, not a licence for this tool to assert the entity, so the codes emitted here stay at 8000 (Revision 2 §2.6, final paragraph).
imaging_features: Intramedullary cord mass, well demarcated, with cyst or syrinx
Cauda equina or filum terminale mass
Diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement coating the cord and nerve roots
Longitudinally extensive expansile cord signal change
Contrast enhancement present
Scoliosis or vertebral remodelling from long-standing cord expansion

diversion_criteria.feature: Age under 3 years
diversion_criteria.reason: Favours an infant-type or embryonal tumour. Tissue is required; do not register a spinal mass in an infant on imaging.

diversion_criteria.feature: Diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement coating the cord and cauda equina
diversion_criteria.reason: Diffuse leptomeningeal glioneuronal tumour presents this way, and so do tuberculous and carcinomatous meningitis. Imaging cannot separate them, and DLGNT needs 1p deletion (Revision 2 §4.3, Métais 2023).

diversion_criteria.feature: Fever, raised inflammatory markers, known tuberculosis or HIV exposure, or a ring-enhancing lesion
diversion_criteria.reason: Spinal abscess and tuberculoma are common mimics in a high-TB, high-HIV setting and are not neoplasms at all.

diversion_criteria.feature: Onset over days, with a longitudinally extensive T2 lesion and little or no mass effect
diversion_criteria.reason: Favours transverse myelitis or tumefactive demyelination rather than a tumour.

diversion_criteria.feature: Vertebral body destruction, an epidural mass, or a dumbbell lesion through the neural foramen
diversion_criteria.reason: Points to a bone primary, a paraspinal tumour or a nerve sheath tumour — none of which is a Group III primary.

diversion_criteria.feature: A known primary tumour anywhere else
diversion_criteria.reason: The spinal lesion may be a deposit. Metastatic disease is coded to the primary at Stage 1, never to the biopsy site.

options.label: A discrete intraspinal mass is present; nothing on the diversion list applies; the report offers no confident tumour type

diagnosis_rendering.comment: Registered on imaging without tissue. Neither the lineage nor the behaviour of the lesion is established, and no spinal entity in this group has an imaging-only diagnostic endpoint.

options.upgrade_path: Biopsy with H&E would reach subependymoma or myxopapillary ependymoma on morphology alone; with GFAP and EMA it would reach spinal ependymoma.

options.label: A discrete intraspinal mass with frankly aggressive features — cord destruction, necrosis, rapid interval growth — and nothing on the diversion list applies

diagnosis_rendering.comment: Registered on imaging without tissue. Malignant behaviour is inferred from growth and destruction on MRI; no lineage is established and no CNS5 entity is reachable.

options.upgrade_path: Biopsy with GFAP, Olig2 and H3 K27M would separate a diffuse midline glioma from a high-grade astrocytic tumour.

options.label: One or more diversion features above apply
options.coding_note: Any diversion feature forces the tissue branch whatever the imaging constellation says. The non-neoplastic gate comes first because three of the six diversion features are mimics that are not tumours.

options.label: The scan shows no discrete mass — signal change, leptomeningeal enhancement or cord swelling only

nodes.question: Is a definitive paraffin histology report in the file, and if not, what did the intraoperative preparation say?
nodes.hint: A frozen section or squash is never the coded diagnosis. If the paraffin report exists, code from that. Only where no definitive histology will ever follow does the intraoperative reading stand on its own — and then it is cytology, not histology.
nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 §3.4. Where no definitive histology follows, the intraoperative diagnosis stands as cytology, basis of diagnosis 5, code capped at NOS, confidence low. It must not be silently promoted to basis 7. ADAPTR places squash and frozen section at RL I alongside H&E, so a site with no IHC still has this capability.

options.label: A definitive paraffin histology report IS in the file — code from that
options.coding_note: The intraoperative impression is recorded as a separate field and is not coded. Jain 2022: frozen section sensitivity 91.43%, squash 88.57% — good, and still not the diagnosis.

options.label: No definitive histology will follow, and the squash or frozen reads 'ependymoma' or describes perivascular pseudorosettes

diagnosis_rendering.comment: Intraoperative squash or frozen section only; no definitive paraffin histology followed. Ependymal morphology was described on a cytological preparation, which cannot support a CNS WHO grade or a molecular type.

options.upgrade_path: Retrieval and processing of the paraffin block, with GFAP and EMA, would confirm the type and give the grade.

provisional_pending.reason: Coded from an intraoperative preparation alone. The paraffin block was never processed or its report is lost, so the diagnosis rests on cytology.

options.label: No definitive histology will follow, and the squash or frozen reads 'glioma' or 'glial tumour' without a type

diagnosis_rendering.comment: Intraoperative preparation only. Glial lineage was described cytologically; astrocytic versus ependymal lineage, grade and H3 K27M status are all unestablished.

options.upgrade_path: Processing the block with GFAP, Olig2, EMA and H3 K27M would separate the ependymal, piloid and diffuse midline branches.

provisional_pending.reason: Cytological glial call with no paraffin section behind it.

options.label: No definitive histology will follow, and the squash or frozen reads only 'tumour' or 'neoplastic cells'

diagnosis_rendering.comment: Intraoperative preparation only. Neoplastic cells were seen; neither lineage nor behaviour was established.

options.upgrade_path: Processing the block would give lineage and, with IHC, the type.

options.label: No definitive histology will follow, and the squash or frozen reads 'high-grade malignant tumour' without a lineage

diagnosis_rendering.comment: Intraoperative preparation only. Malignancy was called on cytology; no lineage was established and no CNS5 entity is reachable.

options.upgrade_path: Processing the block with a glial and an embryonal panel would establish the lineage.

options.label: The squash or frozen shows inflammation, granulomas or gliosis — no neoplastic cells

nodes.question: Before any code is considered: does the file establish that this spinal lesion is a neoplasm at all?
nodes.hint: Benign is not the same as non-neoplastic. Subependymoma, myxopapillary ependymoma and pilocytic astrocytoma are non-malignant and ARE registered. This gate is only for lesions that are not tumours.
nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 §1.7: with non-malignant neoplasms now registered, the non-reportable exit stops being the destination for benign behaviour and is reserved for the genuinely non-neoplastic. In a high-TB, high-HIV setting that is not a rare exit.

options.descriptor: Pyogenic abscess or epidural empyema — pus, neutrophils, organisms
options.reason: A spinal abscess is an infection, not a neoplasm. No morphology code is emitted and the case leaves the registry.

options.descriptor: Tuberculoma, spinal tuberculosis or Pott's disease — caseating granulomas, acid-fast bacilli
options.reason: Tuberculosis of the spine is not a neoplasm. No morphology code is emitted. This is a common mimic of an intraspinal tumour in a high-TB setting and is the reason this gate exists.

options.descriptor: Demyelination — transverse myelitis, tumefactive demyelinating lesion, macrophage-rich lesion with relative axonal preservation
options.reason: A demyelinating lesion is not a neoplasm. No morphology code is emitted. Tumefactive demyelination is biopsied precisely because it looks like a tumour on MRI.

options.descriptor: Syrinx, arachnoid or dermoid cyst, vascular malformation, cavernoma or haematoma
options.reason: A cystic, vascular or haemorrhagic lesion of the cord is not a neoplasm. No morphology code is emitted.

options.descriptor: Gliosis or reactive change only, adjacent to a lesion that was not itself sampled
options.coding_note: The lesion was missed, not excluded. This is an inadequate specimen, not a negative biopsy, and it resolves to the group NOS code at basis 2 with a re-biopsy pending.

options.descriptor: A neoplasm is present — continue to the morphology pattern

nodes.question: Where does this tumour actually arise? A lesion inside the spinal canal is not necessarily a spinal CNS primary.
nodes.hint: Group III covers tumours of the spinal cord and cauda equina themselves. A nerve root tumour, a vertebral tumour, a paraspinal mass growing through a foramen and a deposit from elsewhere all belong to other ICCC-3 groups, and each is coded from that group's own tree.
nodes.coding_note: Every branch here emits no Group III code. Clerk-facing text is in reason, never in coding_note — coding_note is not displayed, so a referral written there arrives with no explanation.

options.descriptor: Arises from a nerve root or is a dumbbell tumour through the foramen — reported as schwannoma or neurofibroma
options.reason: Schwannoma and neurofibroma are peripheral nerve sheath tumours, not CNS tumours, and ICCC-3 places nerve sheath tumours in Group IX (soft tissue and other extraosseous sarcomas). Code this case from the Group IX tree. Do not give it a Group III code because it sits inside the spinal canal — the canal is where it grew, not what it is.

options.descriptor: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumour arising from a spinal nerve root, with or without neurofibromatosis type 1
options.reason: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumour belongs to ICCC-3 Group IX, subgroup IXd. Code it from the Group IX tree and record the NF1 status there.

options.descriptor: Paraspinal, posterior mediastinal or retroperitoneal mass invading the canal — small round blue cell or neuroblastic morphology
options.reason: A paraspinal neuroblastic tumour invading the spinal canal is a sympathetic nervous system tumour, ICCC-3 Group IV, and is coded from the Group IV tree at its paraspinal primary site. Canal invasion is extension, not a second primary.

options.descriptor: Paraspinal soft-tissue sarcoma invading the canal — rhabdomyosarcoma, extraosseous Ewing sarcoma or similar
options.reason: A soft-tissue sarcoma that invades the spinal canal stays a soft-tissue sarcoma, ICCC-3 Group IX. Code it from the Group IX tree at the soft-tissue primary site.

options.descriptor: Vertebral bone primary invading the canal — Ewing sarcoma of bone, osteosarcoma, or a bone lesion of Langerhans cell histiocytosis
options.reason: A malignant bone tumour of a vertebra belongs to ICCC-3 Group VIII and is coded from the Group VIII tree at the vertebral site. Record the bone versus soft-tissue origin explicitly — it is what separates Group VIII from Group IX for Ewing sarcoma.

options.descriptor: Intraspinal or epidural lymphoma — lymphomatous infiltrate on the biopsy
options.reason: Lymphoma involving the spinal canal is a lymphoma, ICCC-3 Group II, and is coded from the Group II tree. Record the compartment (nodal, extranodal or marrow) there — it is what settles the Group I versus Group II split.

options.descriptor: Myeloid sarcoma or chloroma — a granulocytic deposit, usually in a child with known or concurrent leukaemia
options.reason: Myeloid sarcoma is a leukaemic deposit and belongs to ICCC-3 Group I. Code it from the Group I tree and record the marrow findings there.

options.descriptor: Leptomeningeal or intramedullary deposit from a known INTRACRANIAL CNS primary — medulloblastoma, ependymoma or germinoma seeding
options.coding_note: This is still Group III, but the primary is intracranial and this tree cannot code it. There is no branch destination for 'right group, wrong compartment', so the case routes to the unspecified tree, which records the site problem. Go back to Stage 1 and capture the intracranial primary site; the spinal deposit is not a separate primary.

options.descriptor: None of these — the origin of the lesion is not established in the file

nodes.question: What pattern does the H&E section show, and where in the spinal canal does the tumour sit?
nodes.hint: Morphology comes before markers here. Myxopapillary ependymoma and subependymoma are reachable on morphology alone in this compartment, and both must be recognised before any stain is interpreted. Where the tumour sits also matters: the filum terminale and conus are where myxopapillary ependymoma arises.
nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 §4.1: 'Spinal: myxopapillary ependymoma and subependymoma are reachable on morphology; MYCN-amplified is not.' The sublocation captured here is read by sp_mpe_gate. Papillary, clear cell, cellular and tanycytic are morphological PATTERNS in CNS5, not types; only papillary kept a code (9393/3), and it is a legacy string with no diagnostic content.

options.descriptor: Papillary fronds around hyalinised vessels set in a myxoid or mucinous matrix — tumour at the filum terminale, conus medullaris or in the cauda equina
options.coding_note: The classic myxopapillary ependymoma picture in its classic site. GFAP completes the diagnosis at RL II (Revision 2 §4.0).

options.descriptor: The same papillary-and-myxoid picture, but the tumour is INTRAMEDULLARY in the cervical or thoracic cord, not at the filum or conus
options.coding_note: Myxopapillary ependymoma outside the filum and conus is uncommon and the confidence drops accordingly, but the morphology is the type-defining feature and CNS5 does not make the site a criterion.

options.descriptor: Clusters of bland ependymal nuclei in a dense fibrillary matrix, often with microcysts — low cellularity, no mitoses, no necrosis
options.upgrade_path: None required for the type. Satgunaseelan records that RL III surrogate immunohistochemistry is considered unnecessary for subependymoma — H&E alone fulfils the essential criteria.
options.coding_note: The only Group III entity in this tree reachable at RL I. Grade is left null: CNS5 grades subependymoma histologically and this corpus does not print the numeral, so the registrar should set it from CNS5 Table 3 rather than have the tool guess. Subependymoma retains H3 K27me3, which is why it must be excluded on morphology before that stain is read anywhere in this group.

options.descriptor: Perivascular pseudorosettes, true ependymal rosettes, or both — a monomorphic, well-demarcated intramedullary tumour
Ependymal morphology with a clear-cell, densely cellular or tanycytic (spindled, fascicular) pattern
options.coding_note: Clear cell, cellular and tanycytic ependymoma are Related terms of 9391/3 in ICD-O-3.2 and were demoted from subtypes to patterns by CNS5. They change nothing; do not look for a separate code.

options.descriptor: Ependymal morphology that the report calls PAPILLARY — papillary architecture without a myxoid matrix, and not at the filum or conus
options.coding_note: Captures the report's use of the word so 9393/3 can be emitted downstream. 9393 is a legacy string: CNS5 demoted papillary ependymoma to a morphological pattern and it carries no diagnostic content. It is reachable only because a report used the word.

options.descriptor: Piloid pattern — compact bipolar cells with Rosenthal fibres alternating with loose microcystic areas, with or without eosinophilic granular bodies
options.coding_note: The single most consequential branch in this tree. Metais 2023: 25% of paediatric spinal pilocytic astrocytomas are DLGNT. Do not let this close to 9421 without the 1p question being asked.

options.descriptor: Oligodendroglioma-like clear cells with rounded nuclei, with or without a subpial or leptomeningeal distribution
options.coding_note: Oligodendroglioma-like morphology is the first element of the DLGNT recognition set (with Olig2, a neuronal marker, 1p deletion and a MAPK alteration). It routes to the same node as the piloid pattern because the two are the ends of the same problem.

options.descriptor: Diffusely infiltrative astrocytic tumour of the cord — no piloid features, no brisk mitoses, no necrosis
High-grade tumour — brisk mitoses, microvascular proliferation and/or necrosis, astrocytic or undifferentiated
options.coding_note: H3 K27M must be asked here. A diffuse midline glioma can be spinal — CNS5's definition covers pons, thalamus, spinal cord and cerebellum.

options.descriptor: Mesenchymal / sarcomatoid - spindle, pleomorphic or rhabdoid cells with no glial or neuronal differentiation; GFAP and OLIG2 negative where stained
options.coding_note: Added 2026-09-15. Routes to the shared node st_dicer1_sarcoma. Primary intracranial sarcoma, DICER1-mutant is 92% supratentorial with a median age of 6 years, so every compartment that can carry it reaches the node; g3_midline deliberately does not.

options.descriptor: A neoplasm is present but no usable descriptor is recorded, and nothing suggests malignancy

diagnosis_rendering.comment: Tissue was examined and a neoplasm confirmed, but the report records no pattern the classification can act on. Neither lineage nor behaviour is established.

options.upgrade_path: Ask the pathologist for a pattern description. GFAP, EMA and Olig2 would separate the ependymal, piloid and diffuse glial branches.
options.coding_note: Basis 7, not 2 — the tissue was adequate and was examined. 8000/1 is IIIf.

options.descriptor: A clearly malignant neoplasm — mitoses, necrosis, infiltration — but the lineage cannot be determined from the section

diagnosis_rendering.comment: Tissue was examined and shows a malignant neoplasm of undetermined lineage. No glial, ependymal or embryonal lineage was established, so no family-level glioma code is defensible.

options.upgrade_path: A lineage panel (GFAP, Olig2, synaptophysin, EMA, and an embryonal panel) would place the tumour in a family.

options.descriptor: The section shows no neoplasm — inflammation, granuloma, demyelination or gliosis only

nodes.question: Which stains were done on this myxoid, papillary cauda equina or cord tumour?

marker_groups.group_label: Read only to exclude a mimic

provisional_pending.reason: Morphology alone. GFAP has not been performed, so the ependymal nature of the tumour is not confirmed.

nodes.question: What grade, if any, does the histology report give this ependymal tumour?
nodes.hint: Read the grade off the report; do not derive it. CNS5 states that a spinal ependymoma is CNS WHO grade 2 or 3, and nothing in this tool's evidence set supplies a mitotic threshold for the spinal compartment that would let it choose.

options.descriptor: No grade is stated in the report
options.coding_note: The grade field stays null. Revision 2 §7.2: the grade field will legitimately be null for much of this group.

nodes.question: Which stains confirm the ependymal nature of this spinal tumour?
nodes.hint: GFAP with a dot-like or ring-like EMA pattern is the ependymal combination. Nothing on this panel can establish MYCN amplification: MYCN immunohistochemistry has no published sensitivity or specificity and definitive classification requires demonstration of the gene amplification.

RL III surrogate — records the result, cannot classify

grade_resolution.criterion: CNS WHO grade 2 versus grade 3 for a morphologically defined spinal ependymoma (Revision 2 §4.0). CNS5 states the type carries grade 2 or 3; which one is a report finding, not a threshold this corpus publishes for the spinal compartment.

not_stated.reason: The report states no grade. CNS5 grades spinal ependymoma 2 or 3 and no criterion in this corpus lets the tool choose between them, so the grade is omitted rather than guessed.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: EMA would confirm the dot-like or ring-like pattern; MYCN FISH on fresh tissue (RL IV) would establish or exclude spinal ependymoma, MYCN-amplified.

grade_resolution.criterion: ADAPTR histologic grade II versus III for a spinal ependymal tumour reported descriptively (Revision 2 §2.3, §4.0 — 'SP ependymoma, NOS', grade II or III).

not_stated.reason: The report states no grade and no criterion in this corpus lets the tool assign one. Satgunaseelan retains grading because in a resource-limited setting it may be the only prognostic indicator — which is a reason to ask the pathologist, not to infer it.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: GFAP and EMA (RL II) would give the WHO CNS5 diagnosis of spinal ependymoma with its CNS WHO grade. MYCN FISH on fresh tissue (RL IV) would establish or exclude the MYCN-amplified type.

A GFAP-negative tumour with an ependymoma-like architecture is usually not an ependymoma. Metastatic deposits, paraganglioma and nerve sheath tumours all enter the differential here, and none of them is coded from this tree.

nodes.question: What does MYCN testing show on this spinal ependymoma?
nodes.hint: Only demonstrated MYCN gene amplification establishes the type. MYCN immunohistochemistry may help, but definitive classification requires the gene amplification, and no sensitivity or specificity has been published for the stain — so an IHC result is recorded, never classified on.
nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 §4.0: spinal ependymoma MYCN-amplified is RL IV by MYCN FISH; RL III MYCN IHC yields a descriptive diagnosis only. §1.4: 9396/3 is Ependymoma, RELA fusion-positive and is supratentorial — it must never be borrowed for a MYCN-amplified spinal tumour. §7.2 and §7.9: CNS5 Table 3 states no grade for spinal ependymoma MYCN-amplified, so grade stays null on that branch.
