nos_fallback.reason: No MYCN result was selected. 9391/3 is the ependymal family root and the code that carries the descriptive diagnosis 'SP ependymoma, NOS'.

nodes.question: A piloid or oligodendroglioma-like tumour of the cord. Which stains were done?
nodes.hint: Do not close this to pilocytic astrocytoma on morphology. One in four paediatric spinal tumours reported as pilocytic astrocytoma is a diffuse leptomeningeal glioneuronal tumour, and the two cannot be separated on H&E or on this panel — 1p deletion is the discriminator, and it needs FISH.
nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 §4.3 and Métais 2023. DLGNT's recognition set is oligodendroglioma-like morphology plus Olig2 plus a neuronal marker plus 1p deletion plus a MAPK alteration; DLGNT has no ICD-O-3.2 code at all, so it is recorded as an entity annotation against the nearest defensible code. §7.11: no ADAPTR paper covers the glioneuronal tumours or the paediatric-type gliomas, so every resource_level_gate here carries rl_assignment by_analogy.

markers: Diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement coating the cord and cauda equina

resolution_logic.coding_note: Every spinal piloid or oligodendroglioma-like tumour goes to 1p testing where the laboratory can do it, whatever the stains show. This is the whole point of the branch: the markers do not separate pilocytic astrocytoma from DLGNT and 1p deletion does.

diagnosis_rendering.descriptive_diagnosis: Spinal low-grade glial and glioneuronal tumour with oligodendroglioma-like features, NOS
diagnosis_rendering.comment: Olig2 and a neuronal marker are both expressed in a spinal tumour with oligodendroglioma-like or piloid morphology. That combination is part of the recognition set for diffuse leptomeningeal glioneuronal tumour, which cannot be separated from pilocytic astrocytoma without 1p deletion testing. 1p has not been tested. The code emitted is 9421/1 because DLGNT has no ICD-O-3.2 code; it is a placeholder, not the diagnosis.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: 1p deletion by FISH or chromosomal microarray (RL IV) is the discriminator. A MAPK alteration would complete the DLGNT recognition set.

nodes.question: What does 1p testing show on this spinal piloid or oligodendroglioma-like tumour?
nodes.hint: 1p deletion is what separates a diffuse leptomeningeal glioneuronal tumour from a pilocytic astrocytoma. Record the method: FISH and chromosomal microarray agree on 1p in only 45.8% of cases (kappa 0.16) in the one small series available, so a FISH call is worth less than an array call and both are worth more than nothing.
nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 §4.3. DLGNT is a WHO CNS5 entity with no ICD-O-3.2 code at all, so it is recorded with entity_annotation code_status no_code against 9421/1. §7.2: CNS5 Table 3 states no grade for DLGNT, so grade is null on that branch. The 1p FISH-versus-CMA concordance figure rests on n = 11 and is a caution, not a settled effect.

options.coding_note: The diagnosis and the code deliberately differ. DLGNT has no ICD-O-3.2 code, so 9421/1 is emitted as the nearest defensible placeholder and the entity is carried in the annotation. Confidence is medium because the CODE is a stand-in, not because the entity is doubtful. Grade is null — CNS5 Table 3 states none for DLGNT.

options.finding: 1p intact — no deletion (FISH or chromosomal microarray)
options.upgrade_path: None. With 1p intact, the diffuse leptomeningeal glioneuronal tumour alternative is excluded and pilocytic astrocytoma stands.
options.coding_note: Grade is left null: CNS5 does grade pilocytic astrocytoma histologically, but the numeral is not printed anywhere in this tool's evidence set, so the registrar should set it from CNS5 Table 3 rather than have the tool assert it. 9421 is /1 — non-malignant and registered. Do not apply the adult anaplastic-pilocytic-astrocytoma criteria in a child: 77% of cases so labelled were plain pilocytic astrocytoma (Gareton 2020).

options.finding: 1p testing attempted but uninterpretable — hybridisation failed, array failed quality control, or too few scorable nuclei

diagnosis_rendering.descriptive_diagnosis: Spinal low-grade glial and glioneuronal tumour, NOS
diagnosis_rendering.comment: 1p testing was attempted and could not be read. A failed assay is not an intact 1p: diffuse leptomeningeal glioneuronal tumour is neither established nor excluded, and a repeat on fresh or better-preserved material is owed.

options.upgrade_path: Repeat 1p testing. Where FISH failed, chromosomal microarray is the better second attempt — the two agree on 1p in only 45.8% of cases in the available series.

provisional_pending.reason: 1p testing failed. The result is unknown, not negative, and the distinction between pilocytic astrocytoma and DLGNT remains open.

options.coding_note: Basis 7, not 8 — no molecular result was obtained. Deliberately distinguishable from the 1p-intact branch, which is Track A, basis 8 and high confidence.

options.finding: 1p testing not performed or not available

diagnosis_rendering.descriptive_diagnosis: Spinal low-grade glial and glioneuronal tumour, NOS
diagnosis_rendering.comment: Piloid or oligodendroglioma-like morphology in a spinal tumour, with 1p deletion untested. 25% of paediatric spinal tumours reported as pilocytic astrocytoma are diffuse leptomeningeal glioneuronal tumours, and nothing short of 1p testing separates them.

options.upgrade_path: 1p deletion by FISH or chromosomal microarray (RL IV) is the discriminator. Referral to an RL IV centre is highly recommended.

provisional_pending.reason: 1p deletion has not been tested. Diffuse leptomeningeal glioneuronal tumour accounts for 25% of paediatric spinal tumours reported as pilocytic astrocytoma (Métais 2023) and is not excluded by anything on this branch.

nos_fallback.name: Pilocytic astrocytoma
nos_fallback.reason: No 1p result was selected. 9421/1 is the nearest defensible code for a spinal piloid tumour and is NOT a settled diagnosis while 1p is untested — diffuse leptomeningeal glioneuronal tumour has no code of its own and is not excluded.

nodes.question: A diffusely infiltrative or high-grade glial tumour of the cord. Which stains were done?
nodes.hint: H3 K27M must be asked on every one of these. A diffuse midline glioma can be spinal — the CNS5 definition covers the pons, thalamus, spinal cord and cerebellum — and the stain is the whole diagnosis.
nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 correction 9: Diffuse midline glioma, NOS and Diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma are Related terms of 9440/3, so an untested high-grade midline tumour is 9440/3, NOT 9400/3. §4.3: none of the paediatric-type diffuse glioma entities has an ICD-O-3.2 code; each resolves to 9400/3 or 9440/3 by grade with the CNS5 entity as an annotation. §7.11: the paediatric-type diffuse gliomas have no ADAPTR paper, so rl_assignment is by_analogy. The ependymal mis-branch §4.1 warns about — an H3 K27M-positive tumour with ependymoma morphology and dot-like EMA — is prevented structurally: ependymal morphology routes to sp_ependymal_grade and never reaches this node.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: None required for the type. H3 K27M immunohistochemistry is type-defining and has been performed.
resolution_logic.coding_note: The spinal cord is one of the four midline sites CNS5's definition covers. The rendered entity is CNS5 Table 1's spelling, 'Diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27-altered'; the ICD-O-3.2 preferred term on 9385/3 is the older 'Diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27M-mutant'. That divergence is real and is recorded here rather than smoothed over. Grade is left null: CNS5 does grade this type, but the numeral is not printed in this tool's evidence set. Basis 7 — immunohistochemistry counts as histology (Revision 2 §2.6); sequencing would make it 8.

diagnosis_rendering.comment: A high-grade glial tumour of the spinal cord with GFAP expression. H3 K27M was not performed or not recorded, so diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27-altered is not excluded.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: H3 K27M immunohistochemistry (RL III) is one stain and settles the commonest high-grade spinal entity. Methylation profiling (RL V) resolves the remaining paediatric-type high-grade gliomas, none of which has its own code.

provisional_pending.reason: H3 K27M status unknown in a high-grade midline glial tumour.

resolution_logic.coding_note: 9440/3, not 9400/3: Diffuse midline glioma, NOS is a Related term of 9440/3 in ICD-O-3.2. The descriptive string is deliberately 'Diffuse high-grade glioma, NOS' and not 'glioblastoma' — CNS5 states that the term glioblastoma is no longer used in the setting of a paediatric-type neoplasm. The code may be right; the word is not.

diagnosis_rendering.comment: A diffusely infiltrative glial tumour of the spinal cord with GFAP expression and no high-grade features. H3 K27M was not performed or not recorded.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: H3 K27M immunohistochemistry (RL III) — a diffuse midline glioma may be histologically low-grade and is grade 4 regardless. Methylation profiling (RL V) would reach the paediatric-type low-grade glioma entities, none of which has its own code.

provisional_pending.reason: H3 K27M status unknown. A histologically low-grade midline glial tumour may still be a diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27-altered.

resolution_logic.coding_note: Do not use TERT promoter mutation, EGFR amplification or +7/-10 as solitary defining features — cIMPACT-NOW update 11 rules all three out below 40 years, which is every patient in this registry.

diagnosis_rendering.comment: A high-grade tumour of the spinal cord read as glial on morphology alone. No immunohistochemistry was recorded, so neither the glial lineage nor the H3 K27M status is established.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: GFAP and Olig2 (RL II) would confirm the glial lineage; H3 K27M (RL III) would settle the commonest high-grade spinal entity.

provisional_pending.reason: Morphology alone. Glial lineage unconfirmed and H3 K27M untested.

diagnosis_rendering.comment: A diffusely infiltrative tumour of the spinal cord read as glial on morphology alone, with no high-grade features. No immunohistochemistry was recorded.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: GFAP and Olig2 (RL II) would confirm the glial lineage; H3 K27M (RL III) would exclude a diffuse midline glioma.

provisional_pending.reason: Morphology alone. Glial lineage unconfirmed and H3 K27M untested.

nos_fallback.name: Glioma, malignant
nos_fallback.reason: A glial tumour of the cord that the panel does not resolve. 9380/3 is the family-level glioma code and sits in IIId2 at C72.0 and C72.1 — it is IIIb only at C72.3. It is used in preference to 9400/3 because astrocytic lineage has not been demonstrated.

decision_trees.tree_label: Meninges (C70.0, C70.1, C70.9) - meningioma, and what is not a meningioma

nodes.question: A meningeal lesion (C70.0 cerebral meninges, C70.1 spinal meninges, C70.9 meninges NOS). What is actually in this patient's file, and was the specimen adequate for diagnosis?
nodes.hint: Pick the highest tier of evidence that is genuinely in the file. An inadequate or unreadable specimen is not a negative one and never closes to a code here - it leaves this tree. Benign behaviour does NOT leave the registry: this registry registers non-malignant CNS tumours, and six of the twelve meningioma codes are /0 only.
nodes.coding_note: Registrar ruling 14-09-26: register_nonmalignant_cns is true, so the non-reportable exit is reserved for the genuinely non-neoplastic - a tuberculoma, an abscess, demyelination - and is no longer the destination for benign behaviour. Revision 2 §1.3: a malignant-only registration rule would delete 9531-9535 and 9537 outright.

options.label: Referral letter or clinical note only - no pathology report and no imaging report in the file
options.coding_note: Tier 1. Nothing above the family-level code is reachable from a referral.

options.label: Imaging report only - no tissue, no cytology
options.coding_note: ENCR Table 3 permits meningioma 9530/0, 9539/1 and 9530/3 to be registered on imaging at basis 2. This tool emits only 9530/0 without tissue: imaging cannot establish atypia or malignancy.

options.label: Intraoperative frozen section or squash cytology only - no definitive paraffin-section report yet
options.coding_note: Revision 2 §3.4: an intraoperative diagnosis is NEVER the coded diagnosis. Frozen section and squash are RL I. Jain 2022: frozen sensitivity 91.43%, squash 88.57%, kappa = 0.729.

options.label: Tissue with a definitive H&E report - no immunohistochemistry (RL I)
Tissue with H&E and immunohistochemistry (EMA, SSTR2A, STAT6, SOX10, SMARCE1, BAP1 and the like) - RL II-III
options.coding_note: ENCR: immunohistochemistry counts as basis of diagnosis 7, not 8.

options.label: Tissue with H&E, immunohistochemistry AND a molecular, copy-number or methylation result (FISH, MLPA, CMA, WES, methylation array) - RL IV-V
options.coding_note: ENCR: methylation profiling counts as basis of diagnosis 8.

options.label: Specimen INADEQUATE / non-diagnostic - too little tissue, crush artefact, no lesional tissue identified
options.coding_note: Revision 2 §3.3: an inadequate specimen resolves to the group NOS code with a provisional_pending naming re-biopsy, and to basis of diagnosis 2, NOT 7 - the tissue did not yield a diagnosis. That terminal lives in g3_unspecified.

options.label: Specimen technically UNINTERPRETABLE - processing or stain failure, no opinion could be given on the cells present
options.coding_note: Distinct from inadequate and from a negative result. A failed stain is not a negative stain (contract §4, test_result_states). Recorded as not_assessable so the repeat is owed on the record.

options.label: The meningeal origin of the lesion is not established - it is not clear from the file whether the mass is dural, leptomeningeal or intraparenchymal
options.coding_note: Topography is a classification axis in Group III and this tree is entered on C70.x alone. An unestablished site is resolved in g3_unspecified, not guessed here.

options.label: The lesion proved NOT to be a neoplasm - tuberculoma, abscess, meningitis, inflammatory pseudotumour or demyelination
options.reason: Not a neoplasm, so no morphology code is emitted and the case leaves the registry. This exit is for the genuinely non-neoplastic only - in a high-TB, high-HIV setting a meningeal tuberculoma or abscess presenting as a dural mass is not rare. It is NOT the exit for a benign meningioma: this registry registers non-malignant CNS tumours, and 9531-9535 and 9537 exist at /0 only.

nodes.question: What exactly does the referral or clinical note say about the meningeal lesion?
nodes.hint: The wording chooses the code and nothing above the family level is reachable. Do not read a subtype, a grade or 'atypical' out of a referral note - the grade of a meningioma is set by a mitotic count nobody has made yet.
nodes.coding_note: Basis of diagnosis 2, never 1: every CNS row in ENCR Table 3 is basis 2 and no Group III terminal may emit 1. A referral naming a meningioma rests on imaging.

options.label: Note reads 'meningioma' - no subtype, no grade, no pathology report

diagnosis_rendering.comment: Recorded from a referral note. No histology, no mitotic count and no molecular result, so no CNS WHO grade can be assigned and no subtype can be claimed.

options.upgrade_path: An H&E report with an architectural subtype and a mitotic count would give the grade and, where the tumour is grade 1, the subtype's own code (9531-9535, 9537).

options.label: Note names a subtype or a grade - 'atypical meningioma', 'clear cell meningioma', 'grade 2' - but no pathology report is in the file

diagnosis_rendering.comment: The referral names a subtype or grade that the file does not evidence. 9530/0 is the honest ceiling from a referral; record the referral wording verbatim so the case can be re-coded when the pathology arrives.

options.upgrade_path: The pathology report settles the subtype and the mitotic count. A clear cell call additionally needs SMARCE1: interobserver agreement for clear cell on H&E is the worst in the group (kappa = 0.17).
options.coding_note: Do not code 9539/1 or 9538/1 from a referral. Revision 2 §4.15 gates the clear cell branch on SMARCE1, not on wording.

options.label: Note reads only 'dural mass', 'extra-axial mass for investigation' or similar - no diagnosis asserted
options.coding_note: Not a meningioma referral. It must go through the meningeal lesion triage before any code is considered - the meninges carry solitary fibrous tumour, melanocytic tumours, lymphoma and dural metastases as well as meningioma.

nodes.question: Imaging-only registration. Tick EVERY feature below if the report describes it. If any one is missing, or any diversion feature is present, the case needs tissue.
nodes.hint: ENCR Table 3 permits meningioma to be registered on imaging at basis of diagnosis 2. It permits registration; it does not license a grade. Imaging cannot count mitoses, so this route emits 9530/0 with no grade and low confidence, and never 9539/1 or 9530/3.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §6 rule 11: an imaging terminal without histology carries no_tissue, endpoint_verification 'not_verified', basis_of_diagnosis 2 and a non-empty diversion_criteria[]. ENCR also lists 9539/1 and 9530/3 on the meningioma row; both are deliberately not offered here - neither atypia nor malignancy is an imaging finding.
imaging_features: Extra-axial, dural-based mass with a broad dural attachment
Dural tail (enhancing thickened dura trailing from the mass)
CSF cleft or displaced cortical vessels between the mass and the brain
Homogeneous, avid post-contrast enhancement
No intraparenchymal (intra-axial) component

diversion_criteria.feature: Bone destruction (as opposed to hyperostosis), or rapid interval growth
diversion_criteria.reason: Cannot be separated from an atypical or malignant meningioma on imaging, and grade is exactly what this route cannot supply. Tissue is required.

diversion_criteria.feature: Lobulated mass with prominent flow voids, marked restricted diffusion, or necrosis
diversion_criteria.reason: Favours meningeal solitary fibrous tumour, which is a Group IX tumour and leaves this tree entirely.

diversion_criteria.feature: Leptomeningeal (pial) spread rather than a single dural-based mass
diversion_criteria.reason: Favours a melanocytic tumour, meningeal involvement by lymphoma, or leptomeningeal metastatic disease - none of them coded here.

diversion_criteria.feature: A known malignancy elsewhere, at any time
diversion_criteria.reason: A dural metastasis reproduces every feature of a meningioma on imaging. Metastatic disease is coded to the primary at Stage 1, not to the biopsy site.

diversion_criteria.feature: Multiple meningeal masses, or a history of cranial irradiation
diversion_criteria.reason: Multiple and radiation-associated meningiomas are over-represented in children and are more often higher grade; imaging cannot grade, so tissue is required.

diversion_criteria.feature: Intraosseous, orbital or scalp mass with no dural base
diversion_criteria.reason: The meningeal origin is not established; the Stage 1 topography needs re-capture.

diagnosis_rendering.comment: Registered on imaging alone under the ENCR imaging-only exception (Visser 2023 Table 3, meningioma 9530/0 at basis 2). No tissue, so no mitotic count, no architectural subtype and no CNS WHO grade.

nodes.upgrade_path: Tissue with H&E gives the subtype and the mitotic count, and with it the grade and the subtype's own code.

nodes.question: A frozen section or squash cytology was reported. What happened after it?
nodes.hint: An intraoperative diagnosis is never the coded diagnosis. Where a definitive paraffin report exists, enter that instead. Where none will ever follow, the squash stands as CYTOLOGY - basis of diagnosis 5, code capped at NOS, confidence low. It must not be promoted to basis 7.
nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 §3.4. ADAPTR places squash/smear and frozen section at RL I, so a site with no immunohistochemistry still has an intraoperative capability. Jain 2022 paediatric CNS: frozen 91.43%, squash 88.57%, kappa = 0.729.

options.label: A definitive paraffin-section report has since been issued
options.coding_note: Re-enter at the evidence gate with the definitive report. Do not carry the intraoperative impression forward as the diagnosis.

options.label: The squash or frozen called a meningioma, and no definitive histology will ever follow - the block was never processed, or the report is lost

diagnosis_rendering.comment: Intraoperative squash or frozen section only, with no definitive paraffin-section report. Recorded as cytology (ENCR basis of diagnosis 5). No mitotic count and no subtype, so no CNS WHO grade.

provisional_pending.reason: The code rests on an intraoperative preparation. Frozen section and squash cytology agree with definitive histology at 91.43% and 88.57% respectively; the definitive paraffin section is the test that would overturn or confirm this.

options.upgrade_path: The paraffin block, if it can still be found and processed, gives the subtype, the mitotic count and the grade.

options.label: The squash or frozen could not classify the lesion, and no definitive histology will follow
options.coding_note: No diagnosis was ever reached from tissue. Resolved in g3_unspecified at basis 2, not here - a meningioma was never established.

options.label: The intraoperative diagnosis was something other than a meningothelial tumour
options.coding_note: Send it through the meningeal lesion triage - solitary fibrous tumour, melanocytic tumours, lymphoma and metastases all leave this tree.

nodes.question: What does the histology (and any immunohistochemistry) show the lesion to be?
nodes.hint: The meninges are not only meningioma. Solitary fibrous tumour, melanocytic tumours, lymphoma and dural metastases all sit at C70 and none of them is coded from this tree. Settle the line of differentiation before anything else.
nodes.coding_note: Referral text is in `reason` on every refer branch, never in coding_note - a referral written in coding_note arrives with no explanation because the engine does not display it (nodes.md §4, DT master §3F).

options.label: Meningothelial tumour - whorls, syncytial sheets, psammoma bodies, intranuclear pseudo-inclusions; EMA and/or SSTR2A positive where immunohistochemistry was done
The report says only 'meningioma', with no description of the architecture
Patternless spindle-cell proliferation with staghorn (haemangiopericytoma-like) vessels and ropy collagen; STAT6 nuclear expression and/or CD34 positive
options.reason: Meningeal solitary fibrous tumour. It is not a meningothelial tumour and it carries no Group III code. ICCC-3 files 8815 in IXb1, fibroblastic and myofibroblastic tumours, and the C70 sites are inside that subgroup's topography range. Code this case from the Group IX tree, not here. Note the STAT6 result explicitly: it is what separates the two, and a TTF-1-positive meningeal tumour is a solitary fibrous tumour far more often than it is a metastasis.

options.label: Melanin-pigmented or melanocytic proliferation; HMB-45, Melan-A or SOX10 positive
options.reason: Melanocytic tumour of the meninges - meningeal melanocytoma, meningeal melanomatosis or meningeal melanoma. None of them is meningothelial and none carries a Group III code. ICCC-3 files the melanoma morphologies 8720 and 8728 in XId, malignant melanomas, across all topographies. Code this case from the Group XI tree.

options.label: Dense atypical lymphoid infiltrate; a CD20-positive or CD3-positive population dominates the lesion
options.reason: Meningeal involvement by a lymphoma. Lymphomas are Group II wherever they present; 9590 sits in IIe across all topographies. Code this case from the Group II tree. Do not code it as a meningioma because the biopsy came from the dura.

options.label: Carcinoma, small round blue cell tumour or another non-meningothelial malignancy - a secondary (metastatic) deposit
options.reason: Metastatic disease is coded to the PRIMARY, not to the biopsy site. Go back to Stage 1 and enter the primary tumour's own topography; the ICCC-3 group then follows the primary, whatever it is. Group XII is named here only because that is where a secondary deposit with no primary ever established is coded - it is not a claim about this case's primary. Do not emit a meningioma code and do not mark the case non-reportable: it is a real cancer in the wrong file.

options.label: The lesion is intra-axial - within the brain or spinal cord parenchyma, not dural and not leptomeningeal
options.coding_note: The Stage 1 topography that routed the case here was C70.x. An intra-axial lesion is C71.x or C72.x and belongs to a different Group III tree; the site is re-captured in g3_unspecified.

options.label: Mesenchymal / sarcomatoid - spindle, pleomorphic or rhabdoid cells with no glial or neuronal differentiation; GFAP and OLIG2 negative where stained; leptomeningeal or dural attachment
options.coding_note: Added 2026-09-15. Routes to the shared node st_dicer1_sarcoma. Primary intracranial sarcoma, DICER1-mutant is 92% supratentorial with a median age of 6 years, so every compartment that can carry it reaches the node; g3_midline deliberately does not.

options.label: A neoplasm is present but the line of differentiation could not be established on the material available
options.coding_note: NOT a meningioma, so 9530/0 would be a false claim. This is the IIIf case - 8000-8005 - which lives in g3_unspecified. See the build report: g3_unspecified may need a third externally linkable entry for an ADEQUATE specimen that yields no line of differentiation, distinct from an inadequate one.

options.label: Not a neoplasm on review - tuberculoma, abscess, meningitis, inflammatory pseudotumour or demyelination
options.reason: Reviewed as non-neoplastic. No morphology code is emitted and the case leaves the registry. This exit is for the genuinely non-neoplastic only; a benign meningioma is registered.

nodes.question: What does the operation note record about the extent of resection?
nodes.hint: Asked first because Berghaus 2026 ranks it first. In 293 meningiomas aged 0-39, extent of resection was the dominant predictor of progression-free survival with the highest c-index, ahead of WHO grade, methylation class, UCSF class and the integrated risk score - none of which stratified outcome at or below 21 years. It is recorded here; it changes no code and no grade.
nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 §1.7 and §4.15. The registry's upper age bound is 18, so every meningioma in it falls inside Berghaus's 0-21 band and this is the default path, not a special case. Extent of resection is a registry data item, not a coding step - no branch here may change the code.

options.label: Gross total resection (Simpson I-III)
Subtotal or partial resection (Simpson IV)
Biopsy only, no resection attempted (Simpson V)
The operation note does not record the extent, or there is no operation note

nodes.question: What architecture or cytology does the H&E report describe?
nodes.hint: Pick the architecture the report actually names. The subtype chooses the code only where the tumour turns out to be grade 1 - a grade 2 meningioma of any architecture is coded 9539/1 and a grade 3 is coded 9530/3, so the mitotic count comes next whatever you pick here.
nodes.coding_note: 9531-9535 and 9537 exist at /0 ONLY - six of the twelve IIIe5 codes. That is why registering non-malignant tumours matters most in this subgroup (ruling 14-09-26): a malignant-only rule deletes the entire benign meningioma spectrum. The grade 1 / 2 / 3 code triple 9530/0 - 9539/1 - 9530/3 is the one ENCR Table 3 itself prints on the meningioma row.

options.label: Meningothelial - lobules and whorls of syncytial cells
Fibrous (fibroblastic) - spindle cells in a collagen-rich matrix
Transitional (mixed) - whorls with fascicles and psammoma bodies
Psammomatous - psammoma bodies dominate the tumour
Angiomatous - numerous small or hyalinised vessels throughout
Microcystic, secretory, lymphoplasmacyte-rich or metaplastic - one of the variants ICD-O-3.2 lists as Related terms of 9530/0
options.coding_note: These four are Related terms of 9530/0 Meningioma, NOS - they have no code of their own and must not be forced onto 9531-9537.

options.label: The report uses the words 'haemangioblastic meningioma' or 'angioblastic meningioma'
options.coding_note: Re-pointed 2026-09-15. This branch previously graded the case as a meningioma and emitted 9530/0. That asserted a meningioma for a tumour CNS5 says is not one. 9535/0 stays in morphology_entries[] flagged obsolete_term so historical records and alias input resolve, but nothing in any tree reaches it.
options.reason: The words 'haemangioblastic meningioma' and 'angioblastic meningioma' do not name a meningioma. They are the historical term for meningeal haemangiopericytoma, and the WHO Classification of Tumours of the Central Nervous System, fifth edition, retires it outright: “The term hemangiopericytoma has been retired, with the tumor now termed only Solitary fibrous tumor” (Louis DN, et al. The 2021 WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System: a summary. Neuro-Oncology 2021;23(8):1231–1251, p. 1248). Solitary fibrous tumour is 8815 in ICD-O-3.2, which ICCC-3 files in IXb1 — Group IX. On the same page that paper makes meningioma a single type with fifteen morphological subtypes, and neither 'haemangioblastic' nor 'angioblastic' is one of them; neither word appears anywhere in it. Where the tumour is instead a true haemangioblastoma, that is 9161 and ICCC-3 IXd8 — also Group IX. Either reading leaves Group III, so code it from the Group IX tree and stop. A historical record already carrying 9535/0 keeps it.

options.label: Clear cell morphology - sheets of clear, glycogen-rich cells with blocky perivascular and interstitial collagen
options.coding_note: Revision 2 §4.15: the clear cell branch is gated on SMARCE1, not on H&E. Rogers 2016 gives clear cell meningioma near-worst interobserver agreement in the group - focal kappa = 0.17, just above papillary at 0.16, and no agreement at all for the diffuse pattern on 3 cases.

options.label: Chordoid morphology - cords of eosinophilic vacuolated cells in a myxoid matrix
options.coding_note: Chordoid meningioma is a Related term of 9538/1, whose ICD-O-3.2 preferred term is Clear cell meningioma. The code is 9538/1 and the rendered diagnosis says chordoid - that is what the two-track output is for. Chordoid is grade 2 by subtype and is NOT gated on SMARCE1; only the clear cell call is.

options.label: Papillary architecture - perivascular pseudopapillae
options.coding_note: ICD-O-3.2 fixes papillary and rhabdoid meningioma at 9538/3 - the behaviour is a property of the code. cIMPACT-NOW update 8 removed the automatic grade 3 for both. Behaviour and grade are separate outputs here and must not be reconciled by inventing either: the code stays /3 because ICD-O-3.2 says so, and the grade comes from the mitotic count like any other meningioma.

options.label: Rhabdoid cytology - eccentric nuclei with hyaline cytoplasmic inclusions
options.coding_note: ICD-O-3.2 fixes papillary and rhabdoid meningioma at 9538/3 - the behaviour is a property of the code. cIMPACT-NOW update 8 removed the automatic grade 3 for both. Behaviour and grade are separate outputs here and must not be reconciled by inventing either: the code stays /3 because ICD-O-3.2 says so, and the grade comes from the mitotic count like any other meningioma.

options.label: The report itself states the diagnosis is an ATYPICAL meningioma (or a CNS WHO grade 2 meningioma)
options.upgrade_path: Record the mitotic count and the denominator it was made in. Grade 2 requires 4-19 mitoses in 10 HPF of 0.16 mm-squared, or 2.5-12.4 per mm-squared; 20 or more moves the tumour to grade 3.
options.coding_note: Grade 2 is definitional for the diagnosis 'atypical meningioma' in CNS5, so the grade follows the diagnosis rather than the evidence and no grade_resolution is needed. The tool codes what the pathologist reported; it does not re-grade the case.

options.label: The report itself states the diagnosis is a MALIGNANT or ANAPLASTIC meningioma (or a CNS WHO grade 3 meningioma)
options.upgrade_path: Record the mitotic count and its denominator. Grade 3 requires 20 or more mitoses in 10 HPF of 0.16 mm-squared, or 12.5 or more per mm-squared.
options.coding_note: 9530/3 Meningioma, malignant. ICD-O-3.2 lists leptomeningeal sarcoma, meningeal sarcoma, anaplastic meningioma and meningothelial sarcoma as synonyms of this code.

options.label: The report states 'meningeal sarcomatosis' - a diffuse sarcomatous meningeal proliferation

diagnosis_rendering.comment: 9539/3 is an ICD-O-3.2 legacy term. It is not a WHO CNS5 entity, so no CNS WHO grade applies to it and none is asserted. Confirm the diagnosis against the meningeal sarcoma differential before accepting it.

options.coding_note: Reachable only from the report's own wording. Note that 'meningeal sarcoma' is listed by ICD-O-3.2 as a SYNONYM of 9530/3 Meningioma, malignant, while 'meningeal sarcomatosis' is the preferred term of 9539/3 - two different codes one word apart. Read the report's exact wording.

options.label: The H&E report describes no architecture and names no subtype

nodes.question: What does SMARCE1 immunohistochemistry (or SMARCE1 sequencing) show?
nodes.hint: SMARCE1 is the one bidirectional, well-evidenced marker in this tree: nuclear expression is lost in 12 of 12 clear cell meningiomas and retained in 320 of 320 controls - 305 meningiomas of other subtypes plus 15 clear-cell mimics including 4 clear cell ependymomas - with kappa = 1.00 against sequencing. Read the internal control: vessels and lymphocytes must stay positive.
nodes.coding_note: Reachable at RL III. Rogers 2016 puts clear cell meningioma at the worst end of interobserver agreement in the group, so Revision 2 §4.15 moves the clear cell call off H&E and onto SMARCE1. The four answers below are not interchangeable: retained EXCLUDES clear cell, while not done and unreadable leave it open and carry a provisional at the terminal.

prior_probability.interpretation: Berghaus 2026 found SMARCE1 altered in 13.7% of meningiomas at or below 21 years, and clear cell morphology in 15.2% of the 0-21 cohort against 1.4% of the over-39 cohort. A paediatric meningioma is roughly ten times more likely to be clear cell than an adult one, so this test earns its place here in a way it would not in an adult registry. SMARCE1 alteration is recorded by Berghaus as an INTERMEDIATE risk of recurrence - a risk tier, not a grade.

options.label: SMARCE1 nuclear expression is LOST in the tumour cells, with the internal control (vessels, lymphocytes) retained
options.coding_note: Clear cell meningioma is established. The code is 9538/1 and the grade is 2 by subtype unless the mitotic count reaches the grade 3 band.

options.label: SMARCE1 nuclear expression is RETAINED in the tumour cells
options.coding_note: SMARCE1 was retained in 320/320 controls, so a retained result excludes clear cell meningioma. The case continues as a meningioma with no established subtype - it is NOT coded 9538/1 and it does NOT carry grade 2 by subtype.

options.label: SMARCE1 was stained but the result cannot be read - the internal control failed, or the block is exhausted
options.coding_note: Not assessable is not negative. The clear cell call stays open and the terminal carries a provisional_pending naming the repeat; a failed control must never be recorded as a retained stain.

options.label: SMARCE1 was not performed, or is not available at this laboratory
options.coding_note: RL III is not reachable here. The clear cell call cannot be made on H&E, so the terminal falls to 9530/0 with the grade unresolved and a provisional naming SMARCE1.

nodes.question: A papillary or rhabdoid meningeal tumour. Was TTF-1 performed, and with which antibody clone?
nodes.hint: Record the clone before anybody calls this a metastasis. TTF-1 is aberrantly expressed in meningeal solitary fibrous tumour and the rate is clone-dependent: 34.3% with clone SPT24 against 2 of 23 with clone 8G7D3/1 (Wu 2021). A TTF-1-positive papillary meningeal tumour read on SPT24 alone is routinely mistaken for a lung or thyroid metastasis and routed out of Group III.
nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 §4.15 diagnostic trap. The clone is the finding; without it a positive TTF-1 means almost nothing in this location.

options.label: TTF-1 was not performed
TTF-1 was performed and is NEGATIVE
TTF-1 POSITIVE, clone SPT24
options.coding_note: SPT24 is aberrantly positive in 34.3% of meningeal solitary fibrous tumours. A positive result on this clone is not evidence of a metastasis and must not route the case out of Group III on its own. Check STAT6 before reconsidering the line of differentiation.

options.label: TTF-1 POSITIVE, clone 8G7D3/1
options.coding_note: 8G7D3/1 was positive in only 2 of 23 meningeal solitary fibrous tumours, so a positive result on this clone is far more specific for true TTF-1 expression. The differential has to be re-opened at the triage node before a meningioma code is emitted - but a positive 8G7D3/1 is still not by itself a diagnosis of metastasis.

options.label: TTF-1 POSITIVE but the report does not state the clone
options.coding_note: Uninterpretable as it stands. Obtain the clone from the laboratory before any metastasis call; the case continues as a meningioma in the meantime because that is what the architecture says.

nodes.question: Does the report describe brain invasion?
nodes.hint: Under cIMPACT-NOW update 8 brain invasion ALONE no longer yields grade 2. In an otherwise grade-1 tumour with no genetic testing, invasion means the tumour is reported as meningioma, NOS with the GRADE OMITTED - not raised to grade 2. Because of that, 'no invasion' and 'not assessable' grade identically here, and a specimen with no tumour-brain interface costs the case nothing.
nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 §4.15 Tier 0. This is the single largest change from the superseded revision's grading table. Invasion means irregular tongues of tumour within GFAP-positive parenchyma with no intervening leptomeningeal layer; a tumour that merely abuts the brain is not invasive.

options.label: Brain invasion PRESENT - irregular tongues of tumour within GFAP-positive parenchyma, with no intervening leptomeninges
NO brain invasion, in a specimen that does include a tumour-brain interface
Not assessable - the specimen contains no tumour-brain interface, or the report does not address it
options.coding_note: Distinct from 'absent' on the record even though it grades the same way, because invasion alone no longer changes the grade. Do not record an unexamined interface as an examined negative one.

nodes.question: In what denominator does the report state the mitotic count?
nodes.hint: cIMPACT-NOW update 8 states the same two thresholds in two denominators - 4 and 20 mitoses in 10 high-power fields of 0.16 mm-squared, or 2.5 and 12.5 mitoses per mm-squared. A high-power field is NOT a fixed area, so the count has to be read against the denominator the report itself used. Pick that denominator here and the tool will apply the matching threshold.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §2(7): every numeric_gate band carries a unit and the domain sweep runs per unit. Authoring one band list across two denominators is how a count gets read against the wrong threshold.

options.label: Per 10 high-power fields - the report states a field area of 0.16 mm-squared, or states no field area at all
options.coding_note: 0.16 mm-squared is the field area update 8 defines the threshold against, and it is what most reports mean when they say nothing.

options.label: Per mm-squared (or per 1 mm-squared)
Per 10 HPF, but the report states a field area OTHER than 0.16 mm-squared, and the count cannot be converted
options.coding_note: A count made in 0.23 mm-squared fields is a different density from one made in 0.16 mm-squared fields. Rather than read it against the wrong threshold, the grade is left unresolved and the conversion is named as the outstanding step: mitoses per mm-squared = count / (10 x field area in mm-squared).

options.label: The report states no mitotic count at all
options.coding_note: Do not infer a count from wording such as 'brisk mitotic activity' or 'mitoses are rare'. The count IS the gate.

nodes.question: How many mitotic figures did the report count in 10 high-power fields of 0.16 mm-squared?
nodes.hint: Enter the number the report gives. 4 to 19 is the grade 2 band; 20 or more is the grade 3 band. Tick 'not documented' rather than estimating from a description.
nodes.coding_note: cIMPACT-NOW update 8, Tier 0, as restated in Revision 2 §4.15: 'at least 4 and at least 20 mitoses in 10 HPFs of 0.16 mm-squared'. The per-mm-squared form of the same thresholds is authored separately in mn_mitotic_permm2 so a count is never read against the wrong denominator.

nodes.question: Is any molecular, copy-number or surrogate-IHC result available for this tumour?
nodes.hint: If the answer is no, the case closes on its histology - which for a meningioma in this registry is the normal and defensible outcome. Berghaus 2026 found that WHO grade, methylation class, UCSF class and the integrated risk score ALL fail to stratify progression-free survival at or below 21 years, and this registry's upper age bound is 18.
nodes.coding_note: The Berghaus hierarchy is the default path in this tree: extent of resection first, then SMARCE1 / BAP1 / NF2, then 17q. cIMPACT-NOW update 8 molecular grading is an opt-in side branch two nodes further on, marked evidence_population adult - never the primary route (Revision 2 §1.7).

options.label: No - histology and, at most, basic immunohistochemistry. No SMARCE1, BAP1, NF2, copy-number or methylation result
Yes - SMARCE1, BAP1 and/or NF2 by immunohistochemistry (surrogate markers, RL III)
options.coding_note: ENCR: immunohistochemistry counts as basis of diagnosis 7, not 8.

options.label: Yes - sequencing, copy-number or methylation (Sanger, FISH, MLPA, CMA, WES, methylation array; RL IV-V)
options.coding_note: ENCR: methylation profiling counts as basis of diagnosis 8.

nodes.question: Record the paediatric marker panel. The tool asks one marker at a time and stops as soon as the answer can no longer change.
nodes.hint: These are the markers Berghaus 2026 ranks second, after extent of resection and ahead of every adult grading rule. Only SMARCE1 changes the CODE. BAP1 and NF2 are recorded and change neither the code nor the grade. Expected rates at or below 21 years: SMARCE1 altered 13.7%, NF2 altered 37.3%, BAP1 altered 0.6% - so an NF2 alteration is the ordinary finding here rather than a discriminating one, and a BAP1 alteration is worth re-checking before it is acted on. Ki-67 is NOT a grading criterion in cIMPACT-NOW update 8 and no branch in this tree reads it: record it if the report gives it, never use it to upgrade a tumour the mitotic count places in the grade 1 band.
nodes.coding_note: A retained marker and a marker that was never done both fall to the catch-all here, and that is correct because none of these three can downgrade anything - the difference is preserved in the recorded marker states (ruling 11's `nd` answer) rather than in a branch. Berghaus states SMARCE1-altered as INTERMEDIATE and BAP1-altered as HIGH risk of recurrence: those are risk tiers, not grades, and the grade equivalences Berghaus mentions are cited to a paper not held in this library.

markers: SMARCE1 loss (nuclear expression lost in tumour cells, internal control retained)

prior_probability.interpretation: Altered in 13.7% of the 0-21 group (Berghaus 2026), against clear cell morphology in 15.2% of that group and 1.4% of the over-39 cohort. markers: BAP1 loss (nuclear expression lost in tumour cells)

prior_probability.interpretation: BAP1 alterations occurred in 0.6% of Berghaus's 0-21 group - about one patient - and the authors record low case numbers for BAP1-altered tumours as a limitation on definitive prognostic conclusions. nodes.question: What does the copy-number result show for chromosome 17q?
nodes.hint: Last in the Berghaus hierarchy, after extent of resection and the SMARCE1 / BAP1 / NF2 panel. The paediatric meningioma copy-number profile is gain-dominated with chr17q gain, where the adult profile is loss-dominated. It is recorded; it changes no code and no grade.
nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 §4.15 ruling: rank the evidence as Berghaus does - extent of resection, then SMARCE1 / BAP1 / NF2, then 17q FISH or methylation. Note what is NOT asked here: 1p loss carries no prognostic weight in the paediatric cohort, and 1q gain is not branched on anywhere in this tree.

nodes.question: Are cIMPACT-NOW update 8 molecular grading results (1p, 22q, NF2, CDKN2A/B, TERT promoter) in the file, and how were the arm-level calls made?
nodes.hint: The default answer here is the first one. These rules are derived from an adult population - update 8's evidence base has a median age of 58 and explicitly excludes paediatric, radiation-associated and NF2 meningiomas. Berghaus 2026 found CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion and TERT promoter mutations ENTIRELY ABSENT below 21 years; the only cases were aged 33, 36 and 38. If the results exist, record them - but this is a side branch, not the route the tree expects to take.
nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 §1.7 and §4.15. Every terminal reached through this option carries evidence_population: adult. How the arm-level call was made is captured HERE rather than at the grading node because it decides the confidence of every 1p and 22q rule downstream.

options.label: No update 8 molecular grading results are in the file - close the case on its histology
Yes - the 1p and 22q calls were made by CMA, MLPA, WES or methylation copy-number
options.coding_note: Crumley 2026, WES against CMA: 1p 92.86% (kappa = 0.85), CDKN2A 100%, 10q 95.24%, 14q 88.10%, 22q 85.71%. These are the assays the update 8 rules can actually be carried on.

options.label: Yes - but the 1p and 22q calls were made by FISH
options.coding_note: Crumley 2026, FISH against CMA as reference: 1p 45.83% concordance (kappa = 0.16, n = 11), 22q 62.50% (kappa = 0.21, n = 24). Those percentages rest on small per-arm denominators, not on the 113-case series - the 1p confidence interval runs 27.89-64.93 - so this is a warning, not a settled effect size. 3 of 12 update 8 upgrades in that series rested on FISH calls contradicted by both CMA and WES. Every arm-level rule reached from this option is flagged low confidence.

nodes.question: Record the update 8 molecular findings. The tool asks one at a time and stops as soon as the answer can no longer change.
nodes.hint: Every outcome on this node is derived from an adult population that this registry does not contain. Two findings that look like grading criteria are NOT: a hemizygous CDKN2A/B deletion and H3K27me3 loss are both declared insufficient by update 8 and neither changes the grade here, and p16 immunohistochemistry is not a substitute for CDKN2A/B copy-number testing. Berghaus 2026 found CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion and TERT promoter mutations entirely absent below 21 years across 293 tumours, so a positive result on either is surprising enough to re-check before it is acted on.
nodes.coding_note: Two things Revision 2 §4.15 says must NOT be built, and are not: (1) no branch on 1q gain - Landry 2025 proposes 1p loss plus 1q gain explicitly for 'the next iteration' of WHO grading, on 7 grade-1 patients at risk, and it appears in none of the descriptions of update 8 in this corpus; (2) FISH does not carry the 1p/22q rules on its own - where it made the call the rule still fires but the terminal is flagged low confidence. Masui 2026's proposal to stratify on 1p independently of 22q is logged as the minority view and is not built: Landry found isolated 1p without 22q not significant (15 patients, 0.8%), against 1p+22q HR 1.75 (1.06-2.90, P = .03).

A positive result in this registry is therefore surprising enough to re-check before it is acted on.

nodes.coding_note: This node holds every Tier 0 outcome in one flat ordered list so the grading can be audited in one place. It reads only captured state and asks no marker, so its induced branch_sequence.order is legitimately empty (nodes.md). Rule order: BAP1 first (most specific), then by mitotic band with subtype-specific rules ahead of band-only ones, then the update 8 brain-invasion rule ahead of the grade 1 rules so an invasive otherwise-benign tumour has its grade omitted rather than set to 1, then the grade 1 and no-count rules by subtype, then the catch-all. The grade 1 / 2 / 3 code triple is 9530/0 - 9539/1 - 9530/3, which is the triple ENCR Table 3 itself prints on the meningioma row. Every Track A who_diagnosis on this node leads with 'Meningioma', because that is the ONLY meningioma entity in WHO CNS5 Table 1 - CNS5 collapsed the family into one type with fifteen subtypes. The subtype is written as a subtype so it can never be read as a separate CNS5 type. No entity_annotation is authored anywhere in this tree: that construct exists for CNS5 entities recorded WITHOUT a code, and every meningioma subtype this tree can reach has an ICD-O-3.2 code of its own.

decision_trees.tree_label: Unspecified, overlapping or unestablished site - IIIf, with the five-point flag and the ENCR basis of diagnosis

nodes.question: What is in this patient's file, and how far did the diagnosis actually get? Pick the highest tier that applies.
nodes.hint: Every case in this subgroup records five facts: (a) was surgery performed, (b) was tissue sent to pathology, (c) was immunohistochemistry requested, (d) was the result unavailable or never requested, and (e) the ENCR basis of diagnosis. The option you pick sets them. A tumour that was never diagnosed is still a tumour with recoverable facts on it - record what the file has, not "unknown".
nodes.coding_note: IIIf is the subgroup a resource-limited registry reaches most often (Revision 2 section 1.6). Two NOS-rate figures circulate in this project - ~24% of gliomas without methylation, 50-70% of Group III in registries without neuropathology - and neither is traceable to any paper in the library. They are deliberately not encoded anywhere in this tree. The five-point flag is how the registry measures its own gap from its own data instead.

basis_of_diagnosis_rules.source: ENCR, Visser 2023 - the 2022 revised European recommendations, in force from 1 January 2023 (Revision 2 section 2.6).
basis_of_diagnosis_rules.codes_not_in_use_reason: Codes 3 and 6 do not exist. 6 was merged into 7.
basis_of_diagnosis_rules.rule: Take the highest of codes 1-8. 0 and 9 override.

labels.2: Clinical investigation - imaging, endoscopy, exploratory surgery or autopsy, without a tissue diagnosis
labels.5: Cytology - including flow cytometry and liquid biopsy
labels.8: Cytogenetic or molecular, specific to that cancer

basis_of_diagnosis_rules.group_iii_floor: No Group III terminal may emit basis code 1. Every CNS row in ENCR Table 3 is basis 2. A case carrying nothing but a physical examination is basis 2 where imaging exists and 9 where it does not.

codes_unreachable_in_this_tree.1: Forbidden for every CNS case (ENCR Table 3). The floor is 2 with imaging and 9 without.
codes_unreachable_in_this_tree.4: An elevated AFP or beta-hCG refers the case to Group X and stops; ENCR also rules that code 4 is never used alone. So 4 is never the highest code on a case coded here.
codes_unreachable_in_this_tree.8: A molecular result specific to this cancer would have named an entity, which takes the case out of IIIf. A failed or non-contributory assay leaves the basis at whatever the histology gave.

basis_of_diagnosis_rules.separate_from_confidence: ENCR says a registry may register on imaging. It does not say this tool may assign that morphology code with high confidence. basis_of_diagnosis and confidence stay two fields.

nodes.question: A frozen section or a squash/smear is the only pathology in the file. What did it report?
nodes.hint: An intraoperative opinion is never the coded diagnosis. Where no paraffin report ever follows, it stands as cytology - ENCR basis 5 - with the code capped at the group NOS level and confidence low. It must not be recorded as histology, basis 7. In paediatric CNS tumours frozen section reaches 91.43% sensitivity and squash cytology 88.57% (Jain 2022, kappa 0.729) - good enough to guide the operation, not to fix a registry code.
nodes.coding_note: ADAPTR places squash, smear and frozen section at RL I, alongside H&E: a site with no immunohistochemistry still has an intraoperative capability and the tool should use it. nodes.question: Was immunohistochemistry requested on this block, and did a result come back?
nodes.hint: This is points (c) and (d) of the five-point flag. There is no marker grid here on purpose: if a marker had settled the type, the case would not be in this subgroup. Immunohistochemistry counts as ENCR basis 7 - it is read on the histological section and does not establish a diagnosis on its own - so the answer does not move the basis code. It decides whether this case is waiting for a result or has reached its ceiling, and that is what the registry needs in order to measure its own diagnostic gap. A panel that failed is not a panel that was negative.
nodes.coding_note: ihc_counts_as 7 is a declared project default, not an ENCR rule - the recommendation does not address immunohistochemistry at all. Recorded here rather than left to each abstractor.

resolution_logic.coding_note: Never requested, because this laboratory has no immunohistochemistry. The ceiling is a resource fact about the site, not a judgement about the case - and it is the single most useful thing this flag records.
Requested and never performed. Distinct from not_indicated: the gap is in the workflow, not in the laboratory's capability, and it is recoverable from the same block.
Performed, and the result is not in the file. The block was stained and somebody read it; retrieving the report is the cheapest upgrade on this case.

Performed and uninterpretable - failed controls, no staining, unreadable sections. A failed stain is not a negative stain, and this branch must never be collapsed into the one below it: a repeat on a fresh section is owed.

Performed, readable, and it did not classify the tumour. This is the true ceiling case. The suffix stays NOS and not NEC: NEC requires that the test which would have defined the entity was performed and its result did not map to a WHO type, and for a CNS entity that test is molecular, not a panel of stains.

options.reason: Malignant disease with no established primary site is ICCC-3 Group XII, other and unspecified malignant neoplasms, coded at the unknown-primary topography. It is not Group III: 8000-8005 are IIIf only at C70.0-C72.9 and C75.1-C75.3, and the ICD-O codes that would carry the metastatic behaviour, 8000/6 and 8000/9, are outside this group's declaration.

options.label: On review the CNS lesion is a primary after all

nodes.question: If this lesion is not a tumour, what is it?
nodes.hint: This exit is for a lesion that is genuinely not neoplastic. It is no longer the exit for a benign tumour: non-malignant CNS neoplasms are registered (registrar ruling, 14 September 2026) and are coded at /0 or /1. Where tuberculosis and HIV are common these mimics are not rare, and a mass that turns out to be an abscess must leave the registry rather than be coded benign.
nodes.coding_note: Revision 2 section 1.7: the distinction between non-neoplastic and benign was previously blurred and must now be visible in the tree. Every option here emits no code.

options.label: Pyogenic abscess, confirmed on aspiration, culture or resolution on treatment
options.reason: A pyogenic brain abscess is not a neoplasm. No morphology code is emitted and the case leaves the registry.

options.label: Tuberculoma or another granulomatous infection
options.reason: A tuberculoma is not a neoplasm. It is a common mass-lesion mimic where tuberculosis is endemic, and it must not be coded as a tumour of uncertain behaviour. No morphology code is emitted.

options.label: Neurocysticercosis, toxoplasmosis or another parasitic or HIV-associated lesion
options.reason: An infective mass lesion is not a neoplasm. No morphology code is emitted.

options.label: Tumefactive demyelination - multiple sclerosis, ADEM - or progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy
options.reason: Demyelination is not a neoplasm, and tumefactive plaques are biopsied as tumours often enough that this branch is a real one. No morphology code is emitted.

options.label: Infarct, haemorrhage, vascular malformation, arachnoid cyst or another developmental or vascular lesion
options.reason: Not a neoplasm. No morphology code is emitted.

options.label: Nothing in the file establishes either a neoplasm or a specific non-neoplastic lesion - the investigation stopped
options.reason: ENCR registers a case at "at least likely" and does not register it at "possible". Nothing here establishes a neoplasm even as likely, so no code is emitted. This is a held case, not a closed one: re-open it the day a report, an imaging study or an operative note arrives.

options.label: The lesion is a tumour, and the word "benign" is why it arrived at this gate
options.coding_note: Benign is no longer a non-reportable exit. Registrar ruling, 14 September 2026: every ICCC-3 Group III range is declared 0-1,3, so /0 and /1 were always inside the group.

options.label: A neoplasm is documented elsewhere in the file; the non-neoplastic lesion is a second finding

nodes.question: Tissue was reported somewhere and the report is not here. What can be established?
nodes.hint: The basis of diagnosis is what this registry can document, not what a laboratory once knew. With no report in the file the evidence is the imaging and the operative note: basis 2, not 7. Retrieving the report is the one step that changes the code.

Report malignant-only and all-behaviour counts separately: registering non-malignant neoplasms raises the count for a reason that is not epidemiological.

diagnosis_rendering.descriptive_diagnosis: Neoplasm of the central nervous system, NOS
diagnosis_rendering.comment: The tissue was examined by someone and this registry cannot see the result. Basis 2, on the imaging and the operative note, until the report is in the file. No histological grade is recorded. The ADAPTR Roman scale runs II-IV and every value on it presumes a morphological family; a tumour that was never classified cannot be graded, and inventing a grade here would be the one number on the record with nothing behind it.
